England check on Palmer - what are Tuchel's other big choices?
- Published
England have made medical checks on Cole Palmer as Thomas Tuchel considers whether to select the Chelsea forward in his next squad.
The 24-year-old missed all four games during the previous international window with a minor injury.
He completed 90 minutes for Chelsea against Brentford before those matches, and started for the Blues in the first game afterwards.
Tuchel, who names his squad to face Croatia and Spain on Friday, said at the time that Palmer was "playing with discomfort and pain" but was "missing too many opportunities" with England.
Whether he is recalled will be a key theme on Friday. While it is normal for England medical staff to check on players under consideration, it also underlines that Palmer remains on Tuchel's radar despite his stark comments in September.
In addition to deciding whether to select Palmer, head coach Tuchel has a number of other dilemmas to resolve.
Bukayo Saka's injury absence opens the door to another attacker, with his Arsenal team-mate Noni Madueke pushing for a recall following a string of impressive performances.
Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has not played since mid-October and is not fit for selection, while Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah is a major injury doubt.
Defenders Ben White and Djed Spence are pushing for recalls after missing out on the previous squad through injury.
The likes of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice and many others are now stonewall selections - but the intrigue is around the remaining few spots still seemingly up for grabs.
Will some old faces earn a recall or will there be new faces soon pulling on the England shirt? BBC Sport runs down some of the potential candidates for selection.
Josh King
The 19-year-old Fulham midfielder has already been close to a senior England debut.
King travelled to the US as part of the preparation squad before the World Cup, along with Alex Scott, Ethan Nwaneri and Rio Ngumoha.
Scott and Ngumoha have already made their debuts for the senior side and Nwaneri is currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund.
Tuchel said in his last news conference how King is close to a senior call-up and the midfielder has impressed for England Under-21s too.
The biggest challenge for King will be finding a chance to shine in his favoured number 10 position with Bellingham being England's best midfielder and the position being one of real strength for the Three Lions.
Will Lankshear
There is a lack of number nines in the English game and the job of being Harry Kane's understudy is harder than it sounds.
The England captain has just won the Ballon d'Or, likes to play almost every minute for his country and is the captain, record goalscorer and arguably the best player in Tuchel's side.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has been selected in the squads before and since the World Cup but, despite doing well for Leeds, it has not quite clicked for him under Tuchel and he was given just 15 minutes in two substitute appearances in the last window.
Tuchel has started to use Bellingham as the back-up to Kane, but he could opt for more of a prospect in his squad in this shorter window and turn to Lankshear.
The 21-year-old striker, who like Kane started at Tottenham, was sold to Middlesbrough this summer for £20m and has scored 15 goals in all competitions so far this campaign.
He has scored 13 goals in as many games in the Championship, helping Middlesbrough to the top of the division.
He only made his debut for the England Under-21s during the last international window and scored in that game so it would be quite a rise for a player who is not in the Premier League.
Tuchel is aware of Lankshear and with a lack of number nines across the age groups it could be an interesting option for a manager who is not afraid of making big calls.
He did miss Middlesbrough's loss to Wrexham on Wednesday with a tweaked hamstring but could return in time for Saturday.
Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall
The Everton number 10 has turned down call-ups from the Republic of Ireland as he focuses on his dream of trying to represent the Three Lions.
He has been one of the Toffees' standout performers having scored two goals and registered two assists in all competitions, helping Everton to seventh in the league.
Dewsbury-Hall, 28, is a clever technician with an eye for a pass and his ability on the ball would likely suit international football.
But team-mate James Garner, who Tuchel called a mini-Valverde, was called up before Dewsbury-Hall when there were dropouts in the last international break with that showing perhaps he has more to do to get on Tuchel's radar.
Morgan Gibbs-White
Gibbs-White was probably the unluckiest player to be left out of the initial squad last time around when Tuchel got his players together in September.
But the Nottingham Forest midfielder was called up as a late replacement after a number of high profile pull-outs and left a family holiday to join up with the Three Lions squad.
Tuchel values that kind of dedication and referenced the willingness of Gibbs-White, 26, to join up.
The Forest captain featured during every game of the last break although he did not start a game.
But with Forest struggling at the bottom end of the Premier League table - and competing against the likes of Bellingham, Phil Foden, Palmer and Eberechi Eze - the midfielder could miss out again.
- A must pick or unreliable? Tuchel's Palmer dilemma 
  - Published13 hours ago
Ben White
White has been unlucky since he ended his international hiatus to return in March.
The Arsenal defender missed the World Cup with a knee injury that forced him to also miss the Champions League final.
White then missed the first England squad of this campaign with injury, with Tuchel saying the 29-year-old would have been called up if he had been fit, citing his partnership with Saka as potentially good for the Three Lions.
But White has been available for all but one of Arsenal's games this season and would add a quality defensive option at right-back if selected, especially with Reece James missing through injury.
Jordan Henderson
Henderson has not been in the England set-up since the World Cup, where he fell over an advertising hoarding following the win over Mexico in the Azteca Stadium and broke his arm.
Many would have thought the 36-year-old's international career was over but Henderson, then at Brentford, made a move to Chelsea as they looked to add experience to their young squad.
After recovering from the arm injury, Henderson has surprised some to become an important part of the Chelsea midfield, starting five games in a row and scoring twice in a win over Bournemouth, before he missed the Blues' win over Manchester United with injury.
Henderson is a popular figure, respected by staff and players and is again performing at the top level.

"The race is too hard for women. They are simply not tough enough to do it."
Those are the words of Lazarus Lake, race director of the Barkley Marathons - one of the world's hardest ultramarathons which to date, of the approximate 1,000 people who have started, only 20 have ever completed.
Speaking in 2015 and daring for someone to prove him wrong, it took nine years until a British ultra-runner did just that.
Completing the extreme 100-mile course with just one minute 39 seconds to spare of the 60-hour cut-off, Jasmin Paris from Midlothian made history and cemented her name in the ultra-running history books.
But now, increasingly, she is not alone.
Last summer, there was a female one-two for the first time in the gruelling Montane Summer Spine Race from Derbyshire to Scotland. Rachel Entrekin set a new course record and became the first woman to win the Cocodona 250 in Arizona in May, while last month Sophie Woods smashed the overall record by six days to complete the Via Alpina.
It appears female runners are no longer just taking part in ultra-endurance events, they are competing with their male counterparts, breaking records and in some cases, winning races outright.
All of this has prompted suggestions that they are perhaps better suited to these kinds of challenges.
But is there any scientific proof? Do women really have any physiological or psychological advantages in endurance exercise (anything that takes more than six hours)? And if so, could we see more of these records fall in the future?
In running distances up to the marathon, there is on average a 10-12% performance gap between males and females.
Men are generally stronger and built with a bigger aerobic engine.
But as the distance increases, those physical advantages appear to become less relevant and the gap starts to narrow.
The "gender pace gap" diminishes to 0.25% in 100-mile races, according to a study of more than 20 years of amateur ultra-race data conducted by RunRepeat, in collaboration with the International Association of Ultrarunners,
Anything further than 195 miles and women have the potential to be faster.
So why might this be the case?
For Professor Andy Jones, an expert in endurance performance at the University of Exeter, there are three potential physiological explanations why women could perform better over longer distances or durations.
Fat metabolism – women have higher fat stores and burn it more efficiently, giving them a steady energy source for longer.
Muscles – women have more oxygen-efficient muscle fibres, known as "slow twitch", that are better suited for endurance activities.
Fatigue resistance – women retain more strength over hours of endurance exercise.
However, Jones, who played a key role in Eliud Kipchoge's sub two-hour marathon challenge in 2019, is keen to point out that the science in this area is "behind".
"There isn't as much hard evidence as there would be for shorter distances, which have been studied for a long time in quite some detail," he adds.
That is a view shared by Dr Richard Burden, co-lead of female athlete health and performance at the UK Sports Institute, who feels a lot more information needs to be gathered before conclusions can be made.
"At the moment we are speculating … there are definitely some physiological adaptations that you see more in women than men that are favourable for ultra-type events. But those need to be better established and more studies would need to be done."
Physiology, however, only gets you so far. The realities of ultra-endurance exercise - multi-day events, sleep deprivation, extreme terrain and conditions, to name but a few – mean the journey to the finish line is as much mental as it is physical.
And for Sophie Woods, this is where women have the edge.
"It's not necessarily about being the fastest person at the start," she says. "It is about preparation, it is about mental strength and being able to continue to persevere when things go wrong."
During the New Zealand runner's record-breaking run of the Via Alpina, she was forced to expect the unexpected – from disruption caused by wildfires that made her route longer and more dangerous to swarms of horseflies.
"I was so tired and there were so many of them and I wanted to have a complete meltdown and just cry, but I couldn't because if I stopped moving, they started biting me," she says.
"I think women are really good at adapting and continuing and just knowing that once we start something, you've just got to keep moving until you get to the finish."
That view is echoed by Yngvild Kaspersen, who last month became the first woman to win the prestigious Ultra-Trail Mont Blanc CCC race in the Alps twice. She credits her victory to the "mental game" she puts herself through in training.
The Norwegian, who balances life as a professional runner with her job as a GP, also believes female ultra-runners are so strong because camaraderie in the community is unrivalled.
"We're competitors but we're also motivating each other, inspiring each other, pushing each other to do better in the races," she says. "If you see the podiums for the women this year [at UTMB], how close we are and how we're running together out there - that's very special and I'm very proud to be a part of that community and that group of women."
So can we explain why women might be more resilient?
Sports dietitian Renee McGregor, who specialises in athlete nutrition and hormonal health, believes the answer comes from the female body itself.
"The moment women step into puberty, we are dealing with a fluctuating hormonal system," she says. "We never ever give ourselves credit for that, it's just an accepted part of being female. But actually, it is an endurance in itself and I think that's probably where a big part of our resilience comes from."
McGregor, an ultra-runner herself, points to research that suggests female runners display more disciplined and even pacing strategies than men in distance races, maximising on what she terms the female "brain bank".
"I don't think women go into these races without a lot of thought and contingency planning," McGregor adds.
"For example, if you've been through a pregnancy and you've dealt with nausea, if you've had a baby and dealt with the lack of sleep or if you've gone through fertility treatment, you have to go through so much discomfort, but you know you can get through it. And I think it's that knowledge of 'I can get through this, I can find a solution'."
One of the biggest reasons why we cannot talk with any certainty about the potential physiological and psychological advantages that women may have in this field is because participation numbers are low, with women making up roughly only 20% of those on ultramarathon start lines.
Research by SheRACES, a network set up by British ultra-runner Sophie Power to correct gender disparities in running, suggests the reasons for this range from societal perceptions around women's abilities, to concerns around the time needed for training, or access to the right support at the events themselves.
Slowly but surely, however, things are starting to change.
Earlier this year, a trail race in New Zealand became the first UTMB World Series event to achieve a 50:50 gender split, while a leading UK race provider has launched a new initiative to target gender parity at its events.
And now, according to Dr Burden, society is talking about the limits of human performance in a different way too.
"Historically, the majority of the time it [the limits of the human] will be established from male models or male sports," he says. "Now we're starting to break it up into the limits of male performance and the limits of female performance and that's a distinction that needs to be made … but to make better comparisons, we would need more women taking part in ultra events."

When it comes to participation, visibility is key.
Kaspersen describes Rachel Entrekin's historic victory at Cocodona 250, one of the most demanding ultramarathons in the world, as an "inspiration" among the elites to "dare to try".
And at the amateur level, there are those like Emily Fairs, a 22-year-old ultra-runner who documents the realities of her training and races on social media as part of her mission to get more women of all ages on start lines.
"When it comes to endurance training, there are so many components that come into it and that we are fearful of but by seeing another woman do it you think 'right, if she can do it, if she has the tools, she has the knowledge, she has the ability to do all these crazy difficult challenges, then so do I. I'm no different to her. She's no different to me'," says Fairs.
Fairs says she has received thousands of messages from women about how her content has encouraged them to lace up their trainers, and believes recent trends of female success in ultra-running are just the start.
"When the proportion is so low, we have no clue what women are capable of. We're starting to see more women get faster and enter the sport and push themselves and break records. So, who knows where we'll be 10-15 years later down the line?"

Indian security personnel carrying batons and shields and accompanied by riot control vehicles surrounded the site of a planned opposition protest in Delhi on Sunday that is set to demand the resignation of the country’s election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.
Authorities warned of traffic diversions ahead of the protest march and rally that will be led by Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi. The opposition says it expects hundreds of thousands of people to participate in what it says will be a major challenge to the prime minister, Narendra Modi, and his Bharatiya Janata party (BJP).
Opposition parties, student organisations and the youth-led Cockroach Janta party have held near-daily demonstrations since last month demanding that the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, step down over the voter list revision that critics say favours the BJP.
The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Analysts say the youth protests, and growing support for the opposition, form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014. But his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029.
The opposition parties have announced they will hold a nearly 1.5km march on Sunday from central Delhi to the Ramlila Maidan, a ground that is the designated site for their protest rally.
Visuals from news agency ANI showed riot control vehicles and dozens of security personnel armed with batons and shields outside the rally venue, where announcements were being made urging people to ensure smooth traffic movement and cooperate with police officials.
Delhi traffic police said a “large gathering” was expected at the venue, and traffic regulations and diversions would be implemented “as required”.
“People have started coming to participate in this rally ... we have ensured proper arrangements at the venue, and arrangements are also planned on the route of the march that will happen in a few hours from now,” senior police officer Rohit Rajbir told ANI.
The protests demanding Kumar’s resignation erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported in September that his two deputies had raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.
The change, which began last year, removed over 130 million names from voter lists, including 28 million who died, 63 million who relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.
Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party – allegations the poll panel and BJP reject.

The night before I drove the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, I complained to a group of journalists that automakers don’t want to take chances and just build fun, weird cars anymore. About 12 hours later, Mercedes made me eat my words. Outside of all the bombastic extravaganza of the Los Angeles launch, the first true AMG powered exclusively by batteries is a technological triumph that’s as comfortable on the track as it is on the street. And it’s really very good on the track.
Triforce
One of the fundamental problems with EVs is weight. Batteries are heavy, and the old rule about an object in motion tending to stay in motion makes the notion of nimble cornering a difficult engineering problem. Mercedes loves an engineering problem, and after two days behind the wheel of the AMG GT EV, the company has mostly reduced the battery-weight tax that mires EV performance.
On the road and on the track, the vehicle is firmly planted to the roadway. Mercedes says various technologies make this possible. In addition to decades of producing high-performance vehicles, the automaker’s AMG.EA sports-car architecture does a lot of heavy lifting here, constantly adjusting power delivery from the three motors while guiding the Active Ride Control suspension, steering—including up to six degrees at the rear axle—and active aerodynamics to deliver the performance AMG customers have come to expect from a vehicle with the Affalterbach badge on the hood.
An exploded view of the axial flux motor.
Roberto Baldwin
An exploded view of the axial flux motor.
Roberto Baldwin
One of the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe’s battery cells.
Roberto Baldwin
One of the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe’s battery cells.

An exploded view of the axial flux motor.
Roberto Baldwin
One of the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe’s battery cells.
Roberto Baldwin
Of the technology added to the vehicle, the axial flux motors are the most intriguing. Three motors offer a lighter, smaller powertrain that unlocks a host of abilities: two that are 3.1 inches (79 mm) wide in the back, one that’s 3.5 inches (89 mm) wide in the front. Produced by Yasa, which Mercedes bought in 2021, the motors output up to 1,153 hp (860 kW) of peak power in the AMG GT 63, with a nominal output of 711 hp (530 kW) and 1,475 lb-ft (2,000 Nm). During Boost mode, the additional horsepower is available for 63 seconds. Because it’s the AMG GT 63, obviously.
The AMG GT 55’s Boost mode lasts for 55 seconds with a peak output of 805 hp (634 kW). The 55’s nominal output is 557 hp (415 kW) and 1,372 lb-ft (1,860 Nm) of torque. I was able to use the Boost modes of both trim levels multiple times in a row without issue. Indeed, zero to 60 mph (97 km/h) takes about 2.3 seconds and zero to 124 mph (200 km/h) around 6.8 seconds.
Which means on track you can arrive at a corner going really quite fast.
The styling at the rear is… challenging.
Credit:
Mercedes-AMG
The styling at the rear is… challenging.
Credit:
Mercedes-AMG
Thankfully, the AMG GT’s speed can be tamed with regenerative braking and hydraulic brake-by-wire friction brakes: carbon ceramic discs at the front and steel ones at the rear. The system offered incredible stopping power when I decided to push the vehicle on the track and hit the brakes far too late for a tight left-hand corner. The deceleration was solid even as the vehicle was cresting a hill when I applied the brakes.
For drivers looking for an extreme amount of control over their vehicle, there’s the AMG race engineer control system (standard on the 63, optional on the 55) that consists of three dials in the center console: Response, Agility, Traction. They all go up to nine, which is a shame because they could have added two more levels of control. At one, the settings are essentially for new drivers who really shouldn’t be behind the wheel of this vehicle. At nine, everything is turned up to (well, I’d like to say 11) the limit, and it’s a great way to fully unleash everything the vehicle has to offer and spend the day melting tires and struggling to keep the vehicle pointed forward around corners.
On the track, they had us dial it up to seven, which loosened up the rear end and increased throttle response to a level where we easily broke traction at the rear. Regardless of skill level, it’s a fun tool for track days where you can dial in exactly how you want the vehicle to respond.
Twist for fun.
Credit:
Roberto Baldwin
Twist for fun.
Credit:
Roberto Baldwin
Charging forward
Mercedes has moved to an 800 V system with the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe (yes, it’s a long name, but it distinguishes it from the current V8-powered AMG GT). The electrical architecture offers increased efficiencies and quicker charging, but because this is an AMG GT and it’s the automaker’s halo electric vehicle, they’ve decided to push the boat out and enable it to DC fast charge at up to 600kW. In a demo, one of the track AMG GT 63 vehicles hit a peak of 637 kW. At 60 percent state of charge, the car was drawing about 400 kW, and at 79 percent it was still pulling 252 kW. The vehicle went from 17 to 80 percent in about 10 minutes.
Charging quickly is great, but the same cooling technology in that battery pack also allows repeated Boost mode sessions. Mercedes is cooling its cylindrical batteries with a non-conductive oil that first flows by the connectors and then circles back past the center of the battery before returning to be cooled. Mercedes would not comment on the chemistry of the oil it uses, calling it a “secret.”
Mercedes has not shared range targets for the 106 kWh battery pack.
That sound
The driver’s displays are canted toward them.
Credit:
Mercedes-AMG
The driver’s displays are canted toward them.
Credit:
Mercedes-AMG
I want to hate the sound. I want to bat it away as a gimmick meant to appease drivers still clinging to a world of V8 power and loud exhausts.
Instead, the roar of the AMG GT R (C190 generation) comes flooding out of the speakers and activates actuators in the seats, and it’s delightful. It won me over, and the sound placement in the cabin re-creates a sort of mid-engine location for my brain. The result is I’m driving an all-electric AMG with a fake mid-engine V8 noise, and I’m having fun.
The V8 growl appears when you walk up to the vehicle and when it’s turned on. In Comfort, Sport, and Race mode, it’s gone, but in Sport+, it rears its throaty head. When the vehicle is placed into Boost mode, the V8 noise gets louder (as it should).
It doesn’t sound real. It sounds close to real. It’s the difference between listening to a cassette tape of your favorite band and going to see them live. There’s an audio fidelity that’s not quite there, particularly in the low end. But you still enjoy that tape. It’s not necessary, but it’s delightful.
Inside (or finally a use for the passenger screen)
The interior is outfitted with all the luxury bits you expect from a Mercedes. All the usual suspects are there: the quilted door panels, the comfortable seats, and the array of available materials. This includes the screens and, yeah, the passenger screen.
Now this is useful information on a passenger screen.
Credit:
Roberto Baldwin
Now this is useful information on a passenger screen.
Credit:
Roberto Baldwin
But I finally found a use for that screen. It can display all the technical information of the vehicle, including nerdy data points about the amount of Nm a motor is outputting. I’ll never watch a video or play a video game on that screen outside of testing the latest version of MBUX 4.0, but I will stare at it while it shares details about the vehicle.
The seats are very comfortable, and the lumbar support and side bolsters are controlled on screen. Usually I find this annoying, but the level of fine-tuning this affords the driver and passenger is impressive, and I’ll give it a pass. Also, at 6 feet, 3 inches (1.9 m), I fit comfortably in the back seat. The large trunk should allow for a group of four to head out for a nice weekend away. Or maybe pick up the kids from soccer practice.
Kids love fun. Adults love fun. At least they should. Mercedes-AMG built a fun but very expensive vehicle. The AMG GT 55 starts at $145,000 (destination is an additional $1,550) and will be available by the end of the year. The AMG GT 63 starts at $175,000 (destination fee unavailable at this time) and will be available at the beginning of 2027. Regardless of the 401(k) emptying price, the electric coupe should squelch the “all EVs drive the same” discourse.

Leading the Future, the biggest pro-AI super PAC network, is walking away from the midterm elections with just over $20 million still in the bank and a roster of dozens of successful congressional candidates from both sides of the aisle.
At first glance, that looks like a win. The details tell another story, though. The donations went overwhelmingly to safe candidates, and the results in the small handful of riskier races that Leading the Future got involved with indicate that its plans to shape the election fell flat.
When Leading the Future entered the scene in August 2025 vowing to “oppose policies that stifle innovation," it had a war chest of around $100 million thanks to some of Silicon Valley’s biggest tech billionaires—including Andreessen Horowitz, Palantir cofounder Joe Lonsdale, and OpenAI’s Greg Brockman—and was led by major political strategists.
Designed as a “structured ecosystem,” it set a goal of having ”maximum flexibility to engage in the 2026 election cycle and beyond.” The network is made up of 501(c)(4) organizations and federal and state super PACs catering to both sides of the aisle: American Mission largely gives to Republicans, while Think Big largely gives to Democrats. Its structure and overlapping strategists quickly drew comparisons to Fairshake, a massive, well-funded pro-crypto super PAC network that dominated in the 2024 election.
“They came out guns a-blazing, saying, ‘Be afraid, we are going to spend our millions to influence not only how lawmakers legislate us but also against you in your primaries and in your reelection,’” Sacha Haworth, executive director of the Tech Oversight Project, tells WIRED. ”The purpose of that was to bully lawmakers into acquiescence, intimidate them into not sticking their necks out on AI safety or tech industry regulation at all.”
Leading the Future did not respond to requests for comment.
Late last year, Leading the Future took on Democrat Alex Bores, a former Palantir engineer and state lawmaker running in New York’s 12th congressional district on an AI safety platform, spending millions of dollars in attack ads against his primary bid.
“They fully expected to bury him, put his head on a spike, and parade it around as proof that they could,” says Haworth. Instead, Bores’ candidacy became a high-profile proxy war between competing AI philosophies, boosting his profile and platform. The pro-AI safety network Public First, which has significant financial backing from Anthropic, spent $15 million boosting Bores’ candidacy. Though Bores didn’t win, he came second in a crowded primary field to another candidate, Micah Lasher, who campaigned on tech accountability and AI safety.
Leading the Future spent about $26 million in independent expenditures on the primaries alone. But spending tapered off as it headed into the general election, as the network dropped about $10 million in total while overwhelmingly backing candidates in safe races. Its funding also dropped off, with the network reporting zero donations in the second and third quarters.
The strategy seems to have shifted around the same time that stark polling began coming back showing widespread distrust of Big Tech and cronyism in Washington, DC. (An NBC exit poll found that 56 percent of voters said AI and data centers played a “major” role in their vote.)
Backing safe candidates was, simply put, “an influence play,” says Haworth. ”They're trying to ingratiate themselves with incoming members of Congress.”
The co-founder of Public First Action says that the midterms marked a victory for AI safety. “Voters in both parties delivered the same verdict tonight,” says Brad Carson. “This is a crushing blow to the AI industry’s anti-regulatory efforts to buy a Congress that would look the other way.”
Results weren’t great in the riskier races that Leading the Future jumped into.
One of its biggest bets was on Darline Graham, the sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham and an incumbent running to serve a full term in South Carolina. Graham earned the moniker “Data Center Darline” from her Democratic opponent Annie Andrews due to her enthusiastic support of AI and data center expansion. American Mission donated more than $2 million to Graham, who ultimately lost with 46.5 percent in a state that last elected a Democrat to the Senate in 1998.
Of the other toss-up House races that Leading the Future weighed in on, almost all were in support of Republican candidates through the American Mission super PAC. The exception was Democratic Florida representative Jared Moskowitz’s reelection campaign, which it funded through Think Big. Moskowitz won by 13,000 votes against challenger Scott Singer, the former mayor of Boca Raton.
In North Carolina’s 1st congressional district, Leading the Future through American Mission backed Republican Laurie Buckhout, a retired Army colonel who served as an assistant secretary of defense working on cyber policy under President Donald Trump in 2025, in her primary. Guardrails Alliance, another player in the AI safety network, backed her opponent, Democrat Don Davis, who previously cosponsored a bill that would limit tax giveaways for data center development. Davis won.
Leading the Future also backed Aaron Flint, a retired combat veteran, conservative commentator, and former state director for Republican representative Ryan Zinke, who was running in Montana’s first congressional district. Flint conceded to his Democratic opponent Sam Forstag, a Democratic wildland firefighter who landed endorsements from major progressives including Alexandra Ocasio-Cortez and advocated for strict federal oversight of AI. (The Associated Press has yet to call the race.)
American Mission Florida, a state-level super PAC in the Leading the Future network, got $3 million in support of Republican gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds. While both Donalds and opponent David Jolly took nuanced approaches to the AI safety issue, they diverged strongly on the issue of data center expansion, with Donalds opposing statewide bans or moratoriums on data centers.
After Tuesday night, Silicon Valley will be bracing for what’s expected to be a reckoning over the expansive power and freedom it has enjoyed thus far during Trump’s second term. Democrats have vowed to bring Big Tech bosses to Capitol Hill for hearings. Senator Ron Wyden signaled what's to come in a pithy statement on X. “Subpoenas,” he wrote.

Supreme Court refuses to entertain Azam Khan's bail plea in ED case, urges HC to hear matter
Khan was arrested on October 31 in the money laundering case, shortly after he and his son were released from Rampur prison in an alleged dual PAN card case.
The Supreme Court on Thursday refused to entertain Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan’s plea challenging his arrest in a fresh money laundering case filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and urged the Allahabad high court to hear the matter on November 16.
“The high court has been granting you liberty at every stage. We do not want to bypass the high court,” a bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi said.
Khan was arrested on October 31 in the money laundering case, shortly after he and his son Abdullah Azam Khan were released from Rampur prison in Uttar Pradesh in an alleged dual PAN card case. The latest case pertains to alleged misuse of government funds in the construction of the Mohammad Ali Jauhar University that was established in Rampur by Khan. The 78-year-old SP veteran was produced before the special Ghaziabad court and subsequently sent to judicial custody for 14 days.
The top court bench directed the transfer of Khan’s bail petition to the Allahabad high court within two days. It also directed the registrar general of the high court to immediately place the matter before the chief justice, to constitute a division bench for the hearing on November 16. “The division bench is requested to pass order on the prayer for interim relief (bail),” it said.
Appearing for Khan, senior advocate Kapil Sibal alleged that ED has opened 28 new Enforcement Case Information Reports (ECIR) based on predicate offences dating back to 2006. He argued that the whole purpose of arresting his client now is to keep him in custody ahead of the assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh early next year.
“Your argument may have substance but if we say something in your favour it will prejudice the case. We will request the high court to decide on the very first day of reopening after the Diwali vacation. If there is a vacation bench, we will ask the chief justice to consider,” the bench said.
Sibal said the Allahabad high court granted Khan bail on October 29 in the dual PAN card case, but ED officials were already waiting outside the jail before he could walk out.
He cited Khan's age and the 87 previous cases in which he has secured bail. He also pointed out that the latest arrest comes ahead of the state assembly elections scheduled to be held next year.
“They have shown goats and cows as proceeds of crime, does it not shock judicial conscience? And 28 fresh cases have been lodged by ED. It will take years for me to be released in all these matters. This is pure persecution as they want me to die in jail. They knew I would be released by the high court, so they filed a fresh ECIR. This is to make sure in the next elections I am not there,” he said.
The bench told Sibal: “It appears the nub of the ED material is Income Tax proceedings where a substantial amount has been shown as part of the management of the university. Your argument is that it is malafide. There is a substantial passage of time but what the ED plead is that because of your supervening influence, FIR was not registered back then.” It was referring to the SP rule in Uttar Pradesh in 2006, when party leader Mulayam Singh Yadav was chief minister.
The court also said one of the ECIRs is with regard to misuse of Haj Committee funds.
On October 29, Khan was granted bail in the dual PAN case, in which he was awarded a 10-year prison term. The high court suspended the sentence but refused to stay the conviction.

Vietnam withdrew on Monday a proposal allowing children aged 15 to 17 to donate their organs after death following public criticism in a country where deceased donor transplants remain limited.
The Southeast Asian country began kidney transplants in 1992 and performs the most annual transplants in the region, according to state media.
However, the vast majority of transplants in Vietnam rely on living donors. Transplants in many other nations mostly use organs from deceased donors, expanding their donor pool.
Officials in Vietnam say they are seeking to update a 2006 law on organ and tissue donation, aiming to increase life-saving transplants while safeguarding donors.
A draft submitted to the National Assembly last month proposed allowing 15- to 17-year-olds to donate their tissues, organs or bodies after death, provided the child's parent or legal representative consented.
But, after online backlash, officials removed the under-18 donor provision from a revised draft dated Sunday, with the government saying it had accepted recommendations from lawmakers that only legal adults should be permitted to donate their organs.
Dissent is heavily restricted in communist Vietnam, but opposition centred on whether parental consent could adequately protect child donors from pressure or exploitation.
Criticism also focused on a survey of schoolchildren as young as seven conducted in October to gather feedback on the draft law.
The poll prompted questions about whether minors could understand complex medical, legal and ethical issues, state outlet Tuoi Tre News said.
It said "the provision allowing minors to register as posthumous organ donors prompted considerable controversy and differing opinions among the public".
"Taking these concerns into account, the government has revised the draft," stipulating that only people aged 18 or older may donate their organs, Tuoi Tre said.
National Assembly deputy Pham Khanh Phong Lan urged lawmakers last month to oppose allowing child organ donors, saying: "You cannot sacrifice one child to save another."
One Threads user posted on Monday: "The power of public scrutiny has paid off. It is a relief to see this draft proposal rejected."
The newly revised draft still allows living minors to donate regenerative tissue, for bone marrow or stem cell transplants, to family members when no suitable adult donor is available.
The procedure would require health assessments, counselling and consent from both the child and their legal representative.
A draft law is expected to be approved this month.

Bangladesh garment factories close as workers clash with police in pay protests
Police have clashed with garment workers demanding higher minimum wages in Bangladesh, where days of protests have disrupted an industry that employs about 4 million people
DHAKA, Bangladesh -- Police in Bangladesh fired tear gas and used stun grenades on Wednesday to disperse garment workers protesting for higher wages, police and witnesses said.
Hundreds of factories remained shut after days of protests disrupted the country’s garment industry, which earns about $40 billion a year from exports. Bangladesh has some 2,500 garment factories.
Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 takas ($245), up from 12,500 takas. They say rising living costs and inflation have eroded their purchasing power.
The industry employs about 4 million workers, mostly women from rural Bangladesh.
After days of demonstrations in the capital, Dhaka, violence was reported in several industrial areas on its outskirts.
In Fatullah, in Narayanganj district outside Dhaka, dozens of people were injured in clashes between protesters and police, according to media reports. Police fired tear gas and used stun grenades.
Prothom Alo, Bangladesh’s largest Bengali-language daily, reported that police arrested several protesters in Fatullah.
About 100 factories remain shut in Ashulia, in Savar near Dhaka, said Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of Ashulia Industrial Police.
Workers also blocked a major highway in Gazipur district, another major industrial hub.
More than 10,000 police officers had been deployed in Dhaka’s Mirpur area, an epicenter of recent protests, to maintain order, said Mahidul Islam, a joint police commissioner.
The government has responded to the wage demands by forming a new wage board.
The board’s chairman, Syed Azad Subhani, said workers would receive their first salaries under the new pay scale in January.

The State government has released ₹9.86 crore for the modernisation of 16 drug de-addiction centres functioning in government hospitals across Andhra Pradesh, with a focus on strengthening medical treatment, counselling and rehabilitation services for people suffering from substance addiction.
The funds have been released by the Prohibition and Excise Department to upgrade infrastructure and provide advanced medical equipment at the centres.
A statement issued on Friday said the initiative aimed to make de-addiction services accessible at the grassroots level while strengthening specialised treatment and rehabilitation facilities at major regional hospitals. The proposed works include renovation of hospital buildings, restructuring of rooms, installation of glass doors, improvement of electrical systems and provision of modern furniture.
The centres will be equipped with advanced medical devices, including biofeedback machines, breath-testing equipment, multiparameter monitors and ECG machines. Digital information technology facilities will also be introduced to improve healthcare delivery.
Modernisation works will be taken up at 10 government teaching and major hospitals under the Medical Education Department. They include Kurnool Government General Hospital, SVRR Government General Hospital in Tirupati, Guntur Government General Hospital, Srikakulam Government General Hospital, Nandyal Government General Hospital, Rajamahendravaram Government General Hospital, Ongole Government General Hospital, Vijayawada Government General Hospital, King George Hospital in Visakhapatnam and the Institute of Mental Health under Kadapa Government General Hospital.
Of these, Vijayawada Government General Hospital, King George Hospital in Visakhapatnam and the Institute of Mental Health in Kadapa will be developed as specialised Centres of Excellence. These three regional centres will provide advanced medical treatment, specialised addiction care and comprehensive rehabilitation support to people struggling with substance abuse.
Infrastructure at six other district and area hospitals will also be upgraded. They are Anakapalli District Hospital, Narsapuram Area Hospital, Narasaraopet Area Hospital, Chittoor District Hospital, Hindupur District Hospital and Bapatla Area Hospital.
The works at these hospitals will focus on improving buildings and electrical infrastructure and installing modern medical equipment to strengthen de-addiction treatment services.

Quick Answer
To optimize WhatsApp privacy, hide your Last Seen, Online status, profile info, and status sharing under Settings > Privacy. Turn off read receipts, silence unknown callers, restrict group invites, disable link previews, and enable disappearing messages, passkeys, two-step verification, biometric locks, and end-to-end encrypted backups.
I don’t need to specifically tell you about WhatsApp’s popularity. It has billions of users worldwide, and it is the go-to messaging app for many people. Thanks to the network effect, most popular messaging apps haven’t replaced WhatsApp, even with better features and privacy.
One of the biggest reasons most people use WhatsApp, besides the fact that their friends or family are already on it, is that it is free to use. And since Meta owns it, free usually comes with a caveat. And that’s your data and how Meta tracks your WhatsApp chats. Although your chats are encrypted and Meta openly says it won’t use your data for advertising, you can talk to a friend on WhatsApp and still see relevant ads on other Meta platforms like Instagram instantly. Don’t you believe me? Just try it once.
Fortunately, WhatsApp also offers various privacy settings to keep your conversations private, prevent scams, and more. In this ultimate guide, we’ll cover all the privacy settings you need to enable on WhatsApp for maximum privacy. This guide includes all the methods, and I update it frequently and make changes if the features or flow change. Bookmark this page and revisit it anytime to keep your WhatsApp privacy settings up to date.
Table of Contents
WhatsApp Privacy Settings You Should Enable
Hide your Last Seen and Online status
If you care about your privacy and don’t want your people to know when you were online and when you last used the app, WhatsApp allows you to hide the last seen and online status completely
By default, WhatsApp shows the exact time when you last used the app and shows users when you are actually using the app
While these two features let others know when you use WhatsApp, they can also be a downside, especially if others are expecting an immediate reply when they see you online
Fortunately, WhatsApp lets you disable your last seen and completely hide your status. It also gives you more flexibility by letting you hide these from specific contacts, from your contacts, or disable them entirely for everyone.
Here is how to hide your last seen and online status on WhatsApp:
Open WhatsApp on your Android or iPhone and tap the You tab in the bottom-right corner, then tap Privacy.
Now scroll down and, under Who can see your personal info, tap Last seen and online. To hide it from everyone, select Nobody. To show it only to my contacts, select My contacts; to show it only to specific contacts, tap My contacts except.
Hide your profile photo, About, and Links from strangers
Like Last Seen and online status, WhatsApp also shows your profile picture and About to contacts. This also applies to contacts you have outside your network.
Fortunately, like Last Seen and Online Status, WhatsApp also lets you hide your profile photo and About info from strangers, specific contacts, or no one.
How to hide your profile and About from strangers
Open WhatsApp and tap on your profile picture in the bottom right corner of the screen, then tap on Privacy, and then tap on the Profile Picture option
Now you can hide your profile picture, About, and links. To hide it from everyone, set it to Nobody.
If you want to share with all your contacts, select My contacts. To share your profile picture only with specific contacts, tap My contacts except and select the contacts you want to hide your profile picture, About, and links from.
Control who can see and reshare your Status
WhatsApp’s status feature is slowly turning into Instagram Stories. You can now also reshare statuses on WhatsApp. However, unlike Last Seen, this feature is disabled by default.
If you accidentally enabled it and don’t want others to share your status, you can turn off sharing in the status privacy settings. From there, you can also turn off Facebook Stories and Instagram Stories to prevent your WhatsApp status from being shared on other platforms.
How to turn off status sharing on WhatsApp?
Open WhatsApp and tap on your profile picture, and from here tap on the privacy option
Scroll down, tap Status, then turn off Allow sharing and set your status to be visible only to my contacts. You can also remove specific people by setting up exceptions for contacts, or you can share only with specific contacts. From the bottom, also disable Facebook Stories and Instagram Stories to prevent your status from automatically sharing to Facebook and Instagram Stories.
Turn off read receipts
Even if you hide your online status and last seen on WhatsApp, read receipts can still show blue checkmarks when you read their messages. However, if you don’t want them to know you have read their messages and feel pressured to reply instantly, or if you want better privacy and to balance work and personal WhatsApp chats, you can disable read receipts.
Remember, if you disable it, you also cannot see whether they have read your messages. WhatsApp only shows grey ticks even if you read their messages.
Here is how to turn off read receipts on WhatsApp
Open WhatsApp and tap on your profile picture. Scroll down and tap Privacy. Scroll down again and turn off Read Receipts.
Stop strangers from adding you to groups
Another feature that WhatsApp turns on by default is the ability to let your contacts add you to any groups. This includes the number you have temporarily shared with users you don’t know, and once you add it to the group, your number will be shared with everyone in that group, which is a total privacy nightmare.
Fortunately, WhatsApp allows you to stop random people from adding you to groups.
How to stop people from adding you to random groups
Open WhatsApp and tap on your profile picture, then tap on the privacy option
Scroll down and tap on Groups, then select who can add you to groups. However, WhatsApp doesn’t let you set nobody as an option, but you can still do it by selecting My contacts except and selecting all contacts.
Silence calls from unknown numbers
Since WhatsApp primarily requires your phone number to create an account, once your number is exposed, anyone can contact you on WhatsApp. This is why many of us often receive spam business calls.
However, you can silence unknown calls so that you won’t get notified of random spam calls.
How to silence unknown callers on WhatsApp
To do that, open WhatsApp, tap on your profile picture, and tap on the privacy option
Now scroll down, tap on Calls, and enable the Silence unknown callers option
Make new chats disappear automatically
WhatsApp now supports disappearing messages, which deletes chats from both the sender and receiver after a set time. WhatsApp allows you to enable disappearing messages for individual chats or for the entire WhatsApp for up to 90 days
This is especially useful if you don’t want the other person to save your chats.
Since WhatsApp keeps your messages forever even if you delete your own copy, the other person’s phone still has everything.
When you turn on disappearing messages, WhatsApp also prevents the other person from taking a screenshot and reminds you when they try to save a specific chat.
How to enable disappearing messages on WhatsApp?
Open WhatsApp, tap your profile picture, then tap Privacy. From here, tap on Default message timer and select how many days you want to set for WhatsApp. You can select up to 90 days or even 24 hours.
If you want to turn on disappearing messages for individual chats, open the new chat and tap on the three-dot menu on the top right corner of the screen, select disappearing messages, and select the timer
Keep WhatsApp photos out of your gallery
By default, WhatsApp saves all photos you receive to your media gallery, including sensitive and personal ones. Even if you lock WhatsApp, anyone can see the photos you received by opening your phone gallery. This also uses your data to automatically download them and increases your storage usage.
WhatsApp allows you to turn off automatic media download and also lets you stop showing media directly from your photos app
How to stop WhatsApp from automatically saving media
First, you can turn off automatic media downloads. To do that, open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner, then scroll down and tap Storage and data.
From there, scroll down and tap Media auto-download, then select all three: when you are using mobile data, when you are connected to Wi-Fi, and when roaming. Then disable all download options, including photos, audio, video, and documents. This prevents files from auto-downloading on Wi-Fi, mobile data, or while roaming.
How to stop WhatsApp from showing media in your device gallery
Open WhatsApp, tap your profile picture, scroll down, tap Chats, then under Chat settings, disable Media visibility.
Turn on two-step verification with a password
WhatsApp also supports two-step verification to prevent your account from getting hacked. While WhatsApp sends a six-digit SMS code for verification, someone with access to that code can log in to your WhatsApp account. However, you can set a second verification method, such as a password, to prevent anyone from accessing your WhatsApp.
Here is how having two-factor authentication adds better security for your WhatsApp account.
Here is how to set two-step verification with a password on WhatsApp
First, open your profile picture in the bottom right corner of the screen, tap on account option, and tap on Password
Now create a new password. Tap Create password and create a new password.
Once you add two-factor authentication, remember to add a recovery email. This is especially useful if you lose your network; your email acts as a secondary verification method, where WhatsApp sends a code to your email instead of sending a verification SMS.
Create a passkey for phishing-proof login
WhatsApp also added support for passkeys; if you’re not sure what a passkey is, we have explained it in a detailed guide.
Passkeys use your fingerprint or Face ID for authentication instead of depending on SMS or passwords. Setting up passkeys lets you log in to your WhatsApp account using your device ID, which is unique to you.
But it also comes with downsides: if someone else has registered a Face ID or fingerprint, they can also log in to your WhatsApp account, so keep note of it.
How to enable passkeys for your WhatsApp account
To enable passkeys, open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner, then tap Account. From here, under the Login and Security section, tap on Passkeys. Then follow the on-screen instructions to create a passkey.
Turn on security notifications
Next, enable security notifications on your WhatsApp account so WhatsApp notifies you if someone switches phones, reinstalls WhatsApp, or changes linked devices. This could also mean someone else accessed their WhatsApp account and signed in on a new device. Turn on security notifications and confirm with the other person why the security key changed.
How to enable security notifications on WhatsApp
To do that, open WhatsApp on your phone. Tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen, then tap Account. Scroll down, tap Security notifications, and turn on the option that says Show security notifications on this device.
Check linked devices and log out unknown sessions
WhatsApp lets you link and use your account on multiple devices. However, this could also mean someone could link your account to their device without you knowing. So, if you are suspicious about your account activity, you can check linked devices and sign out of any you don’t recognize.
How to check linked devices and log out of unknown devices on your WhatsApp account
Lock WhatsApp with your Biometrics
WhatsApp includes a native app lock feature that lets you lock it with your fingerprint or a pattern. WhatsApp also lets you lock immediately or after a set time. WhatsApp also recently rolled out a new feature to lock WhatsApp Web chats. So, I have made a detailed guide on how to lock WhatsApp on WhatsApp Web. You can watch the video below or follow the detailed steps in this guide.
How to lock your WhatsApp account with your fingerprint or Face ID
Lock and hide your most private chats
WhatsApp also lets you lock individual chats, not just the app. This way, you can lock or hide your most private chats. Here is how.
However, Locked Chat uses your device’s biometrics to lock chats. And if you cannot unlock the chat for any reason, you cannot get those messages back. Your only option is to clear the messages and unlock the chat, which you can do by going to Settings > Privacy, tapping Chat Lock, and tapping Clear Chat Lock. To lock the chats, follow the guide below.
Open WhatsApp on your device and, if you want to lock multiple chats on the home screen, select the chats you want to lock, tap the three-dot menu, and tap Lock chat. You can also do it for individual chats right here only.
Turn on Advanced chat privacy for sensitive chats
While disappearing messages remove your chat after a set period, you can turn on Advanced Chat Privacy for chats with sensitive content. This stops the other user from sharing or exporting your chats, and the media used in the chat won’t be saved in that person’s gallery. It also blocks the new Meta AI used in the chat itself.
Here is how to turn on Advanced Chat Privacy on WhatsApp
Hide your IP address in calls
WhatsApp also supports voice calls. Direct calls can connect your phone to another person’s phone, which can reveal your IP address and, in turn, your location. However, WhatsApp allows you to hide your IP during calls. Here is how.
How to protect your IP address in calls
Open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen, then tap Privacy. Then scroll down, tap on Advanced, and enable the option that says ” Protect IP address in calls.
Disable link previews
WhatsApp also supports link previews, which show a preview of the website content. However, to do that, your phone connects to your website and sends a request from your IP address.
So it can easily reveal your phone’s IP address to the website, along with your location. You can also turn off link previews, which prevents those fancy images websites use for spam calls.
How to disable link previews on WhatsApp?
Open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Scroll down and tap on Privacy. From here, scroll down again, tap Advanced, and enable Disable link previews.
Block floods of messages from unknown accounts
WhatsApp also introduced a new feature that blocks messages from unknown accounts. It blocks unknown accounts that send you high volumes of messages, which is especially useful if you receive frequent spam texts or your WhatsApp is being bombed with multiple messages.
How to block a flood of messages from unknown accounts
Open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Tap Privacy, then tap Advanced again, and turn on the option that says Block unknown account messages.
Encrypt your chat backup
WhatsApp relies on Google Drive for your WhatsApp backup and iCloud on iPhone. However, by default, your chat backup isn’t encrypted.
You can turn on end-to-end encrypted backup with a passkey, password, or 64-digit key so third-party servers, including Google, can’t read your backup.
Here is how to encrypt your chat backup on WhatsApp
Open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen, then tap Chats. From here, scroll down and tap Chat backup, then scroll down again and tap End-to-end encrypted backup.
Here, you can turn it on and then use your passkey. Remember, you’ll need this passkey whenever you back up your WhatsApp with this data. You can also use a password or a 64-digit key.
Limit what Meta AI can do with your data
Like any other app, Meta also offers AI features that let you summarise and read messages and also chat with Meta AI. However, because these AI chatbots can’t use your data publicly, Meta uses Private Processing features, which it says process your data privately for those AI features.
However, both of the AI features, including Private Processing features and web search, where Meta AI can search the web based on your queries, are turned off by default. If you turn them on, you can turn them off by default to prevent Meta AI from using your data, even though it is processed privately.
Here is how to turn off the private messaging feature and that switch on WhatsApp
Reserve a username to keep your number private
Recently, WhatsApp introduced usernames on the platform, so instead of your phone number, you can create and share a username and let others contact you through it.
However, your phone number still verifies your account, but for better privacy, you don’t need to reveal it when sharing your WhatsApp account with others. You can also restrict who can message you using your username through a secondary verification method. I have covered in detail how to find your WhatsApp username.

Use Strict account settings if you’re a high-risk target
If you are a journalist, activist, or public figure, Meta offers Strict Account Settings to help protect your account’s security and privacy. Here is a clear breakdown of the difference between standard settings and Strict Account Settings and how to enable strict account settings for your WhatsApp account.
How to enable Strict Account Settings on WhatsApp?
Run the built-in Privacy Checkup
WhatsApp privacy settings can be confusing for beginners since the platform is used by people of all ages. However, WhatsApp also offers a built-in Privacy Checkup tool that provides a step-by-step process to help you enhance your WhatsApp account’s privacy.
It includes details such as choosing who can contact you, controlling your personal info, the ability to add more privacy to your chats, adding more protection to your account, and much more

During World War II, physicists on the Manhattan Project worried that the Nazi German nuclear program might achieve the first nuclear bomb before the US and its allies. That’s not what transpired, but historians have debated just how close the Germans came to achieving criticality in their last attempt at building a reactor: the B8 pile. Werner Heisenberg, who led that effort, claimed that they were close and had only needed a little more uranium. But according to a paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences Nexus, that was not the case: the project simply didn’t have sufficient uranium and heavy water to build a working bomb, given the design they were using.
This particular research started in 2013, when University of Maryland physicist Timothy Koeth—a co-author on the new paper—received the gift of a mysterious heavy metal cube from a friend. He instantly recognized it as one of the uranium cubes used by German scientists in their unsuccessful attempt to build a working nuclear reactor. Only 14 such cubes are known to exist today.
In 2019, we reported on Koeth’s quest to track down the cube’s origins, as well as several other similar cubes that had somehow found their way across the Atlantic. At the time, Koeth and his partner in the quest, then-graduate student Miriam “Mimi” Hiebert, had tracked down ten such cubes around the US. For instance, the Smithsonian Institute had a German uranium cube in storage. They tracked a third cube to Harvard University, where it was regularly passed around to students in introductory physics classes as a curiosity.

Blue Origin plans to do its next New Glenn rocket launch in January 2027, according to CNBC and the Financial Times, which cite a memo from CEO Dave Limp sent to staff. The new timeline follows a May launchpad explosion that damaged Blue Origin’s New Glenn launchpad ahead of a flight that would have brought Amazon Leo satellites into space.
Blue Origin’s next launch now won’t happen until 2027
Blue Origin had been aiming for a launch at the end of this year after a launchpad explosion in May, but now it’s reportedly targeting January.
In October, Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos told Fox News that the company was aiming for a December New Glenn launch, joking that it could be “probably December 31st.” The new, revised launch window is “about 10 days later than Blue Origin’s earlier launch target,” CNBC reports. Limp also reportedly cited bad weather as having an effect on the launchpad rebuilding process.
“This small adjustment doesn’t diminish what we’ve accomplished or the importance of the work still ahead,” Limp wrote in his memo, per CNBC and the FT. “Returning New Glenn to flight remains our top priority — it’s worth it.”

Srinagar, Nov 5: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis on Thursday said it intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the group at the Medina region, home to one of Islam's holiest cities.
The announcement came just minutes after the kingdom's civil defence agency warned of potential danger in the area near the strategic port of Yanbu, Hindustan Times reported.
It was unclear if the two events were connected.
"Air defence intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Medina region," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said in a post on X.
The Houthis rejected any suggestion they were targeting the city, saying such accusations were a "blatant and grave falsehood".
"Our operations target only its oil facilities and military bases," the group said in a statement.
Later, the coalition said it had shot down a drone in Eastern Province, a focal point of Saudi Arabia's oil industry. The province's Dammam airport has been a frequent target of attacks.
The Houthis have repeatedly said their forces would not target the holy cities of Mecca or Medina in their ongoing campaign against the kingdom.
Among their attacks on airports, energy infrastructure and military sites, they have targeted the port of Yanbu on several occasions in recent months.
"A warning has been issued by the National Early Warning Platform in Yanbu Governorate to alert of a potential danger," read a statement published by the agency online.
Yanbu, on the Red Sea, is the terminus of the East-West Pipeline that allows Saudi oil to bypass the blockaded Strait of Hormuz.
The port and pipeline have played a key role since the outbreak of the Middle East war, helping Riyadh ship crude and fuel to global markets.

The Duchess of Sussex’s estranged half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, has been named as a “person of interest” in the Philippine authorities’ inquiry into child sexual abuse image allegations made against her father, Thomas Markle Sr.
The country’s interior and local government secretary, Jonvic Remulla, told a press conference in Manila there were “signs that point that the son is involved in the crime as well”.
He added that Markle Jr, 60, who alerted local police and the FBI to images he found in his father’s belongings, was not yet being treated as a suspect. His alleged involvement is not thought to be directly linked to the material he handed to the police.
More than 7,000 photos and one video – all of under-age males and females of Asian, Latin and European descent, with some as young as 10 and 11 – were uncovered, Remulla said.
He described the images as “the most deplorable displays of impunity towards sexual activity that I have ever seen”.
Markle Sr, 82, who is estranged from Meghan, has reportedly been moved into a care home for dementia patients in the US where he is now living.

He added: “We will know in the next few days.”
Markle Sr, who returned to the US from the Philippines in May, has admitted paying for sex in the Philippines but he has strongly denied possessing child abuse imagery, and suggested he had been “set up”. His son remains in Cebu City in the Philippines.

Markle Jr reported his father after claiming to have found four storage boxes at his father’s home in the Philippines containing “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sex abuse images.

Troops deployed to secure Jakarta trial as tensions remain high over wiretap scandal
Indonesian authorities have tasked thousands of police and military personnel to secure a court appearance of former President Joko Widodo, as tensions remain high in the capital over a wiretapping scandal involving senior police officers
JAKARTA, Indonesia -- JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Indonesian authorities tasked thousands of police and military personnel to provide security Thursday for a trial involving former President Joko Widodo, as tensions in the capital remained high over allegations that top officers had been involved in intercepting the current president's telephone conversations.
Three senior generals have already been detained in the wiretapping scandal, including Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who had been named chief of staff to President Prabowo Subianto last month.
Listyo previously served as national police chief under Widodo, though the former president has not been implicated in the wiretapping investigation. There are allegations that Cabinet officials, politicians, journalists, civil society leaders and business executives were also subjected to unauthorized surveillance.
After losing two presidential races to Widodo, Prabowo aligned himself with the popular leader and campaigned as his successor, choosing Widodo’s son as his running mate in a move that fueled concerns about a growing political dynasty in Indonesia’s young democracy.
Widodo and Prabowo were once close political allies, with Widodo backing Prabowo’s successful 2024 presidential bid, but their relationship has come under increased scrutiny amid signs of a growing rift since Prabowo took office.
Neither has commented on the wiretapping case.
Retired police Gen. Oegroseno, a former deputy national police chief, told the Forum Keadilan TV podcast on Wednesday that investigators should examine all possible lines of command behind the wiretapping, including whether any directives originated from Widodo.
“Investigators should not hesitate to question a former president if necessary,” Oegroseno said. “The motive behind the alleged wiretapping operation must be fully uncovered under the leadership of the current police chief.”
The wiretapping operation could also constitute a serious human rights violation and could be used to intimidate critics and weaken civil liberties, said Usman Hamid, Amnesty International's executive director in Indonesia.
“This is not merely about the alleged wiretapping of the president,” Hamid said in a statement. “Authorities must disclose who else may have been targeted and investigate the full impact of the operation.”
Police allege the unauthorized wiretapping took place between 2025 and 2026, after Prabowo had been elected and while Listyo was still national police chief. National Police Legal Division head Sonta Nasution and Eko Hadi Santoso, a senior instructor at the National Police Education and Training Institute, were also detained.
Authorities have called in more than 20,000 troops to Jakarta, and on Thursday said that 6,770 police and military personnel had been deployed to secure Widodo's hearing. Widodo was called to testify in a defamation trial stemming from allegations that he used a fake university diploma. The trial is unrelated to the wiretapping case and Widodo denied the diploma allegations.
As he arrived Thursday morning at the East Jakarta District Court, the former president was welcomed by hundreds of his supporters chanting messages of encouragement.
The presidential palace has said the wiretaps were being considered an “act of treason” that endangered state interests, but has not linked the deployment of troops to Jakarta to the case.
East Jakarta Police chief Alfian Nurrizal said that the deployment for the hearing was a precautionary measure due to potential security risks and large crowds, and that most of the forces were being held on standby.
Indonesian military spokesperson Maj. Gen. Muhammad Nas previously said that the deployment of the 20,000 marines and other personnel to Jakarta was a “normal occurrence."
Despite the number of troops sent to Jakarta, there has also been no visible military presence on the streets and authorities have said most are being held in reserve in barracks and other facilities.

Italian chef fired after refusing to put pineapple on pizza

An Italian chef sacked from a Brisbane restaurant had refused to put pineapple on a pizza because it was an "insult to his culture".
Davide Tamburella was fired from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in May, a fortnight after a meeting with management who had a string of complaints about the chef's behaviour.
Among them were Tamburella's refusal to provide ham and pineapple pizza for guests at a function. At the time, the chef had stated that any direction from management "need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture".
The details came to light after the chef went to Australia's Fair Work Commission claiming he had been unfairly dismissed.
In its ruling released on Tuesday, the commission noted that Tamburella's refusal to put pineapple on the pizzas was because "he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture".
It also noted that it was the third time Tamburella had refused to use the fruit on pizzas in the past four years.
He had previously requested his boss to "check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza".
The state of Queensland, where the restaurant is located, is considered Australia's pineapple heartland and produces all of the country's commercially-grown pineapples.
On the Sunshine Coast, visitors regularly stop to take photos next to The Big Pineapple, a heritage-listed 16m-tall fibreglass model of the fruit, which has become a local landmark.
Other concerns were raised about Tamburella using foul language, his communication style and "escalation of frustration in the workplace".
The ruling also detailed an incident at work in April this year where Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand when he struck a metal hand rail.
Tamburella had been hoping the restaurant would sponsor a visa for him that allows skilled workers to be permanent residents.
However after his sacking, the restaurant ended that process, the tribunal heard.
He lost his unfair dismissal claim on the grounds that the application had been filed too late, according to the ruling.
The restaurant's managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was "more to this story than a pizza topping".
The BBC has approached Tamburella for comment.
On the chef's LinkedIn profile, he describes himself as someone who, throughout his career, has focused on "delivering exceptional food" and "improving business performance".
Three months ago he posted a "letter for chefs" with the theme "respecting the ingredients".
The LinkedIn profile states he now works at another Brisbane restaurant. A BBC check has found that pineapple is not on that restaurant's menu.

How Antonelli 'blew everyone away' to make Formula 1 history

Just after Kimi Antonelli clinched his first title to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen were united in their assessment of his achievement.
"Incredible," they both said. Coming from the two most successful champions on the current grid, the men who are first and third in the all-time list of F1 record-holders, it meant something.
That Antonelli shared the Mexico City Grand Prix podium with these two titans meant something, too.
To Antonelli, firstly, who said: "I will definitely frame the picture and put it in my house because it's just an incredible moment. "There are going to be others," said 1996 world champion Damon Hill, commentating for BBC Radio 5 live.
"I don't see anything else other than him getting better and better. He's going to have to go through hard times as well, but no one is going to doubt his incredible talent."
No one indeed. Not any more, anyway.
