Addressing social media debates over the scientific validity of Temple's eponymous brain-monitoring wearable, founder Deepinder Goyal issued a statement directed at “Concerned Indian Doctors”, asserting confidence in the R&D behind the wearables. Goyal pointed out that Temple had already spent $30 Mn on its development, including $20 Mn of his personal money. He also noted that the company is raising funding from its employees and customers. “Selling a few thousand devices recovers a small fraction of this investment. A scam that pays nothing is not a scam anyone would run,” the CEO wrote in his post. Goyal further said the product’s 14-day no-questions-asked return policy would validate its product in the market. On questions over Temple’s credibility and scientific validation, he argued that many wearable makers initially relied on internal studies before publishing external validation. He said the company would release pre-prints before peer-reviewed publications and it expects independent studies to emerge once the device becomes available more widely. In a follow-up post, Goyal also said, “Temple is a fitness tracker, and wellness device. We are not a medical device,” adding that the device hasn’t been clinically validated. Important to highlight that pre-orders for the wearable officially opened on November 1, with a hefty listing price of ₹85,000. Units are hand-made to order and expected to begin shipping roughly three months after purchase, starting in early 2027. What Doctors Say About Temple? For context, several medical experts had criticised Temple over its claim that a wearable sensor placed near the temple can reliably measure cerebral blood flow. Hepatologist Dr Cyriac Abby Philips, popularly known as The Liver Doc, published an Instagram carousel calling the product “the biggest health scam and wellness fraud in India,” saying the device can only detect when blood rushes to one’s face. Gurugram-based gastroenterologist Dr Zubin Sharma also noted that blood flows to the brain via arteries in the neck and back of head, not the temple. Additionally, many on social media pointed out that studies published on Temple’s website were not peer-reviewed, and were funded and conducted by the company itself. They also raised questions about the validity of Goyal’s Gravity Ageing Hypothesis, which links the long-term effects of gravity on blood circulation to ageing. In fact, Dr Philips doubled down on the criticism of Temple in a reply to Goyal's latest post, calling out Temple's claims of reading blood flow to the brain and the company's explanation of its proprietary 'Entropy' score. The Temple Journey So Far Goyal’s move into brain-monitoring wearables has been taking shape through a series of bets on longevity research. This began with his personal research initiative Continue Research, which he referred to as his personal health and wellness venture back in 2024. The initiative remained largely under wraps for over a year before unveiling its first hypothesis, Gravity Ageing, in November 2025. The hypothesis proposed that gravity's effect on cerebral blood flow (CBF) could be an overlooked contributor to human ageing. Temple emerged around the same time as a commercial extension of this research. Inc42 first reported in November 2025 that Goyal was exploring a wearable device company focused on health monitoring. The device, which he had been seen wearing near his temple, was being used experimentally to measure blood flow to the brain in real time. “I left the Eternal CEO role to chase purpose with Temple. This is not about money. I have enough of it to last for generations. My incentives are fully aligned with getting the science right. I am not staking a reputation earned over 20 years on making a quick buck,” Goyal said. On the product front, Temple has been developing a wearable that sits on the forehead near the temple and tracks signals associated with cerebral blood flow. Goyal revealed a smaller version of the device in August, claiming it was less than half the size of its earlier iteration. It has worked with contract manufacturers Zetwerk and Ethereal Machines to scale production, while retaining some manufacturing capabilities in-house. The startup began taking shape as a standalone venture earlier this year. In February, Temple raised $54 Mn (around ₹493 Cr) in a seed funding round at a post-money valuation of approximately $190 Mn. The round was led by Goyal, who invested a little over ₹100 Cr, with participation from Steadview Capital, Peak XV Partners, Vy Capital, Info Edge Ventures, among others. More than 30 employees also participated in the round. Temple subsequently expanded its ambitions beyond hardware. In July 2026, it acquired London-based longevity medicine practice Longevous for an undisclosed amount, bringing clinical and scientific expertise into the business.

India's cybersecurity watchdog CERT-In has issued a critical warning to entities in the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) sector over an escalating campaign of AI-driven cyberattacks targeting payment and disbursement APIs. In an advisory dated November 4, 2026, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) identified the threat actor behind the campaign as 'CRAFTY FALCON', describing it as an AI-assisted financial threat actor that uses machine intelligence to identify targets, execute attacks at machine speed and exploit victims' own payment and disbursement APIs to initiate unauthorised fund transfers. Banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), fintech companies and other financial services entities have been warned of the growing threat. CERT-In's Computer Security Incident Response Team-Finance (CSIRT-Fin) said the campaign has witnessed a significant escalation, with successful attacks continuing to be reported across the financial services ecosystem. The agency has urged all BFSI entities to treat the campaign as an immediate and continuing threat. Repeat Attacks Despite Remediation A key concern highlighted in the advisory is the threat actor's continued targeting of financial entities that had already received earlier restricted advisories and undertaken remediation measures. According to CERT-In, some of these organisations have been deliberately targeted again, including cases where remediation was incomplete. The attacks have also been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other periods of reduced monitoring, potentially delaying detection and response. CERT-In's analysis identified the use of multiple publicly available AI-driven offensive security tools in the campaign. These include the ARTEX family of large language model (LLM)-based tools, PentAGI, an autonomous multi-agent AI penetration testing system, and the Cairn attack search engine, alongside the CyberStrikeAI framework. These tools can execute complete attack chains autonomously, generate and refine large volumes of customised attack scripts in rapid succession, and adapt their payloads based on responses from targeted systems. The supporting attack infrastructure also changes frequently, with IP addresses rotating within hours to days. CERT-In said infrastructure fingerprints and detailed detection rules have been shared with affected entities through restricted advisories. AI Agents Pose Growing Cybersecurity Risks The latest advisory follows another critical warning issued by CERT-In in October, when the agency flagged attackers using publicly available agentic AI tools to conduct financially motivated intrusions into Indian organisations. The watchdog warned that autonomous AI agents, ostensibly deployed for research and evaluation, had accessed live systems without authorisation, reading business records containing personal data and confidential information. Meanwhile, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has also warned banks, NBFCs and fintech startups about the growing use of AI agents by cybercriminals to perpetrate financial fraud. The agency said it had uncovered multiple individual cases in which malicious agentic AI systems exploited compromised financial systems to execute unauthorised transactions involving amounts running into crores of rupees. CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities In Tata Motors' Connected Vehicle Apps Separately, CERT-In has flagged multiple vulnerabilities in select versions of Tata Motors' iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev connected vehicle applications, which could allow attackers to access sensitive credentials and vehicle-related information. The agency identified four vulnerabilities, including hardcoded service account credentials, API keys and authorisation tokens within the applications; inadequate validation of URLs and origins loaded through the apps' WebView component; authentication tokens being recorded in application logs; and improper implementation of SSL certificate pinning in the network security configuration. CERT-In has urged users to update their applications to the latest versions of iRA 2.0 (version 26.8.2) and iRA.ev (version 26.9.1). The applications provide access to connected vehicle functionalities, including vehicle status updates, health monitoring, trip details and remote vehicle commands.

AMD reported third-quarter revenues on Tuesday with a record $13.4 billion, an increase of 45 percent year over year, as data center business nearly doubled and the company’s gaming segment cratered.
AMD CFO Jean Hu said, “We expect revenue to be approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3%. The middle point of our guidance represents approximately 66% year-over-year revenue growth, primarily driven by the acceleration of our Data Center segment.” AMD says its Q4 revenue projections are up another 27 percent from this quarter’s results. As reported by Tom’s Hardware, Intel’s Q4 guidance places revenue estimates between $15 billion and $16 billion. That means that if both companies land where they expect to at the end of the fourth quarter, AMD would exceed Intel’s revenue for the first time in history.
The data center segment of AMD’s business was up 97 percent year over year, with a record $8.5 billion. AMD attributes the growth to demand for its EPYC line of enterprise server CPUs, along with the launch of the Instinct MI450 series GPUs. Sales of AMD Ryzen mobile chips led growth in the Client business, which includes desktop Ryzen processors and posted $2.95 billion in revenue, up 7 percent year over year.
Gaming revenue fell sharply for the company, posting a 40 percent drop in revenue at $773 million, which AMD attributes to “lower semi-custom and graphics revenue.” Operating margins in AMD’s data center business expanded from 25 percent to 34 percent, with operating income surging 168 percent to $2.88 billion.
Embedded segment revenue, or all the SoCs, FPGAs, and boards under AMD’s umbrella that go into other hardware, was $1.1 billion, up 29 percent. AMD attributed this growth to gains made in the “aerospace and defense, automotive, communications, and industrial end markets.”

Offering incentives to industries that employ more women and assistance for investments in plant and machinery, as well as a fixed timeline for approval of projects, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in West Bengal on Thursday (November 5, 2026) announced a new investment promotion policy.
The West Bengal Investment Promotion Policy, 2026 that comes into effect from May 9, 2026 the day when the first BJP government in the State took office, offers up to 120 % assistance to a thrust sector unit in a priority area on the share of fixed capital investment (FCI) made in plant and machinery.
The announcement of incentives marks a policy shift for West Bengal, the fourth most populous State in the country, as the previous Trinamool Congress government had passed the Revocation of West Bengal Incentive Schemes and Obligations 2025, retroactively scrapping three decades of industrial incentive schemes and subsidies.
“The previous government had cheated the industrialists,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said while unveiling the much-awaited policy document for the revival of industries in the State. The Chief Minister said that West Bengal will try to emerge from the “bad experiences” as far as industry was concerned of the previous two regimes.
“We will neither have a forcible land acquisition policy like the Left Front nor will we have a flawed land policy like the Trinamool Congress, asking industries to buy their own land without support from the government,” Mr. Adhikari said.
Under the policy of ‘jobs come first’, the State government has announced extending substantial employer EPF contribution reimbursements, leading with 100% reimbursement for women and transgender employees in MSMEs for 10 years, 75% for women in eligible service units and robust support for large and strategic industrial projects.
The ceiling for the amount of assistance given on the share of (FCI) made in plant and machinery is 100 % for regular units, 110 % for units in thrust sectors or priority areas, and 120 % for thrust-sector units located in priority areas. The assistance will cease when the applicable ceiling is reached or 10 years after commercial production begins, whichever is earlier.
The State government has identified several sectors as thrust areas, such as semiconductors and electronics, green hydrogen and waste-to-energy, emerging digital technologies, EVs and batteries, defence and food and marine processing, among others.
On the fixed timeline for approval of projects, the State government has also announced a 30-day delivery of certificates of intent, a 45-day timeline for certificates of eligibility and a dedicated relationship officers for large projects.
The policy promises a waiver of surcharges on renewable energy open access until March 2030, and sick and closed industrial units that can be revived will receive special assistance. Non-profits, such as hospitals and universities who invest more than ₹100 crore can keep at least a quarter of their capacity fee, for groups the State notifies for 10 years along with extra benefits.
The Chief Minister, who interacted with captains of industry during the launch of the policy, sought their opinion on whether they had witnessed any change in the past five months since the BJP government came to power. “If industrialists cooperate with the government, the government will always stand by them and protect their interests,” he said.
One of the promises made by the BJP during the West Bengal Assembly polls 2026 have been to revive industrial fortunes of the State, a commitment that has turned out to be its biggest challenge.
Mr. Adhikari said that he has ended “ended extortion” and added that his government has been “positive about industrialisation and an industry-friendly atmosphere in Bengal”. The State’s Industries and Commerce Minister Tapas Roy and Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta were also present at the launch of the investment promotion policy.
While the Chief Minister assured that the concerns about land acquisition for industry will be addressed, senior officials of the State government said that a GIS-mapped land inventory for industries is being prepared. The State government is likely to have a fresh policy as far as making land for industries was concerned.
Mr. Adhikari said the government had already handed over land to 33 business groups and was in a position to meet the current demand for industrial plots of around ₹1 lakh crore over the next few months.

Color us nostalgic.
Sony has brought back the MDR-3-series headphones that debuted in 1979 alongside the Walkman TPS-L2 cassette player.
Originally called the “MDR-3L2,” the first Walkman headphones were known for their sleek, adjustable gray plastic headband, which extended via metal sliders and ended in signature orange, circular ear cushions. The lightweight, on-ear headphones are a contrast to the bulky headsets that are popular these days, which use wide, cushioned headbands for long-term comfort and large earcups that can support big drivers and are often heavily padded for noise isolation.
The new MDR-3R (note the slightly different name) headphones look just like the originals and come with orange and blue ear cushions.
New headphones are often wireless these days, but the MDR-3R continues the wired tradition of the MDR-3, with an essential twist: a USB-C connector.
“The MDR-3R has been redesigned for modern use while preserving the experience value of freely taking music out into the world, which the original MDR-3 helped popularize,” Sony’s announcement says.

Democrats’ takeover of the House and Senate promises greater scrutiny of the Trump administration’s immigration agenda. But with the President’s executive powers intact and several major policy battles already before the courts, H-1B workers, Indian students and H-4 spouses may have to wait for relief.
The Democratic Party’s victories in the US midterm elections have changed the balance of power in Washington, with the party securing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. But for millions of immigrants, international students and foreign professionals, particularly those on H-1B visas, the more important question is whether the change in Congress will translate into a change in immigration policy.
The answer, according to immigration attorneys and policy experts, is far from straightforward.
Democrats have secured at least 54 seats in the 100-member Senate and, in the preliminary House tally, at least 231 seats against 141 for Republicans, with several races still being counted. The results give Democrats control of both chambers for the first time during President Donald Trump’s current term. The new Congress, the 120th, takes office on Jan 3, 2027.
The change gives Democrats considerable powers of oversight and the ability to scrutinise the administration’s immigration policies. But it does not give them the power to automatically reverse executive orders, presidential proclamations or regulations already issued by federal agencies. That distinction is central to understanding what the election could mean for legal immigration.
Cyrus Mehta, an immigration attorney, cautions against expecting an immediate change in direction. Notwithstanding the midterm results, he says, the President retains the authority to issue regulations and policies through executive action.
“While there may be oversight committee investigations into ICE excesses and abuses, and DHS racial profiling, I think the administration will pretty much carry out its immigration agenda,” Mehta says.
He believes the administration will continue to rely on executive powers, regulations and policy memoranda, particularly because passing major legislation in the Senate generally requires overcoming the 60-vote threshold.
“Congress may be able to question the administration regarding the justification for the $100,000 H-1B fee for hiring workers from outside the US, but its authority is limited to just that: holding hearings and asking questions. The administration will continue to implement rules and policies,” he adds.
Ashwin Sharma, a Jacksonville-based attorney, points out that a presidential proclamation can be revoked by the President who issued it or struck down by a court. A final regulation can be undone through new rulemaking or a Congressional Review Act resolution, although the President could veto such a resolution.
Sharma adds, “What the new majorities actually hold is the power to deny appropriations to specific rules, the power to investigate and subpoena, and, in the Senate, the power to decline nominees and judges. Those are real, and they should take the most reckless anti-immigration tactics off the table. But they do not reverse the immigration agenda. Washington changed who holds the gavel, but not who holds the pen: for the next two years, immigration policy will be drafted in the West Wing and redlined in the federal courts.”
Rajiv S. Khanna, managing attorney at Immigration.com, offers a more detailed account of the tools available to the incoming Democratic majority. Congress, he says, can narrow the authority delegated to the executive through legislation, prohibit particular fees or write programmes such as OPT and H-4 employment authorisation into statute.
But there is a significant obstacle: the presidential veto. A bill must be signed by the President to become law, unless Congress secures a two-thirds majority in both chambers to override a veto.
Khanna believes Democrats could instead use spending legislation to attach restrictions on funding for particular immigration policies. They can also use congressional oversight to demand documents and testimony from officials responsible for implementing controversial measures.The Congressional Review Act offers another possible route for challenging certain final agency regulations. It allows Congress to pass resolutions of disapproval through an expedited process, although such a resolution still faces the possibility of a presidential veto. Proposed regulations and presidential proclamations are not covered in the same way.
Duden Freeman, a former senior official with the US Department of State (DOS), similarly cautions that a change in congressional control should not be confused with comprehensive immigration reform. “While the shift in Congress indicates increased accountability and oversight of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and DOS, I don’t expect most visa policies to change drastically,” she says.
“Everything the administration does that is not in line with the Constitution is taken to the relevant courts anyway,” Freeman says. She adds that real immigration reform may be easier to pass with a Democratic Congress but harder to secure with Trump in the White House.
For Doug Rand, a former senior official with DHS, the courts may prove to be the more consequential check on the administration’s immigration policies.
“The most important check on Trump’s immigration actions may not be the new Congress, but rather the courts. The original $100K H-1B fee was already blocked by a federal judge, and similar attempts to restrict legal immigration will likely meet the same fate,” Rand says.
The question, therefore, is not simply what Democrats can undo after January 3, but which of the administration’s policies can survive legal scrutiny.
H-1B: One fee blocked, another proposed
The H-1B programme is likely to remain among the most closely watched areas of immigration policy, particularly for Indian technology professionals and the employers who sponsor them.
The Trump administration’s $100K payment requirement for certain new H-1B petitions has encountered substantial legal resistance. A federal court in Massachusetts vacated the policy implementing the payment in June 2026, and the First Circuit declined to suspend that ruling in July. A second federal court in California blocked the fee in Sept. The administration has extended the underlying presidential proclamation through Sept 2027, but the fee remains blocked under the relevant court orders.
However, a separate proposal could create another financial hurdle. DHS has proposed a $103K fee for certain cap-subject H-1B petitions through formal rulemaking. As of the date of this draft, it remains a proposal rather than an implemented fee.
Kripa Upadhyay, an immigration attorney and partner at Buchalter, says: “While Congress could increase scrutiny and try to restrict the administration’s ability to collect the proposed H-1B fee by attaching a condition to government funding legislation, it cannot simply stop the separate regulatory process.”
Snehal Batra, managing attorney at NPZ&B, makes a similar point, noting that the administration is pursuing many of its immigration priorities through executive action and agency rulemaking rather than legislation.
“The President retains significant authority over immigration and can direct agencies like DHS, USCIS and ICE to pursue enforcement and regulatory priorities. While Democrats can increase oversight through hearings and investigations and make it more difficult to pass new restrictive legislation, they cannot simply undo existing executive actions. As a result, I expect the administration to continue advancing its immigration agenda through the executive branch, with many of the key battles playing out in the courts through challenges under the Administrative Procedure Act rather than in Congress,” she explains.
Proposed increase in prevailing wages for H-1B and PERM positions
Another concern is the proposed increase in prevailing wages for H-1B and employment-based green card programmes.
Currently, wages are pegged to four levels at roughly the 17th, 34th, 50th and 67th percentiles of market wages. The Department of Labor (DOL) proposes to raise these thresholds significantly. Entry-level (Level I) wages could rise from the 17th percentile to the 34th percentile, aligning them with what is currently considered mid-level pay. The DOL estimates that the changes would increase the average certified wage by about $14,000 per year per position.
Mitchell Wexler, senior counsel at Fragomen, a global immigration law firm, offers an important political qualification. “While Democrats may resist certain fees and restrictions on foreign students, Wexler believes that increased wage minimums for H-1B and employment-based green cards, as well as broader authority for employer enforcement, could find support among some congressional Democrats. “Those aren’t one-party issues as a rule,” he says.
PERM: More scrutiny for employers and green card applicants
Employment-based green card applicants could face another challenging period if the proposed changes to the PERM labour certification process move forward. The Department of Labour (DOL) is considering changes to recruitment requirements and additional protections for US workers, particularly in situations involving recent layoffs. The proposed overhaul had recently cleared White House review.
There is also concern over the suspension of PERM processing involving eight major employers, including Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini.
The incoming Congress could demand explanations from the Department of Labor, according to the attorneys. Upadhyay says: “Congress can’t end the investigation. It can, however, demand the evidence behind it, question why only some companies were singled out, and probe the process. The most likely route to relief is a legal challenge by the companies themselves.”
F-1 students: Is the US becoming a less attractive destination?
For international students, particularly those from India, two policy changes are of concern: the proposed elimination of Duration of Status and the proposed fees for Optional Practical Training (OPT). The Duration of Status rule was finalised but blocked by a federal court before it could take effect. It would replace the existing framework with fixed periods of admission, subject to extensions.
DHS has proposed charging $70,000 for an initial OPT recommendation and $30,000 for subsequent periods, including STEM OPT extensions. Universities would be required to pay the fee before recommending a student for OPT and could potentially pass the expense on to students or employers.
On this front, Khanna believes that the House Oversight Committee is where a Democratic majority can make itself felt fastest. Under House rules, the committee may investigate any matter at any time, even one assigned to another committee. It can compel testimony and the production of documents by subpoena. Officials involved in the $100,000 fee, the OPT fee and the EAD backlog could therefore be called to testify under oath, while the internal analyses behind these measures could be demanded.
Immigration attorneys also believe litigation could be the quickest way to challenge the proposed OPT fee.
H-4 spouses: Uncertainty over work authorisation
The automatic extension of Employment Authorisation Documents (EADs) has ended for renewal applications filed on or after October 30, 2025. DHS subsequently issued a final rule making the change permanent.
Khanna points out that Senate Democrats have already filed a resolution, S.J.Res. 99, against the interim version of this rule. However, the resolution would still require the President’s signature to take effect.
The next concern is the possibility of eliminating the H-4 EAD programme altogether. Batra says: “Because the H-4 EAD has existed for more than a decade, DHS would be required to do more than simply change its mind. The agency would need to acknowledge its policy reversal, provide a reasoned basis for the change, and address the significant reliance interests of H-4 families and their employers. Given the program’s longevity and the economic impact of rescission, any attempt to eliminate H-4 work authorisation would likely face substantial legal and procedural hurdles.”
What changes on January 3?
The incoming Democratic Congress will have more opportunities to scrutinise the administration’s immigration actions. Hearings, investigations, subpoenas and funding negotiations could put pressure on federal agencies.
But the attorneys do not expect the new congressional majority to automatically reverse the administration’s immigration agenda.
Upadhyay believes that, for the immediate future, the courts and the presidential veto will matter more than the congressional majority.
“Where House oversight can do the most good is on pretextual delays. This administration has been assassinating legal immigration by slowing it to a crawl, without changing a single rule. Since Dec 2025, when the State Department ordered an online-presence review of every H-1B and H-4 applicant, consulates in India have cut daily interviews and cancelled appointments wholesale. Individuals are now offered H-1B interview dates more than six months out, and H-4 spouses often find no appointment at all. At USCIS, a standalone H-4 EAD renewal is taking more than a year, and with automatic extensions gone, every month of delay past the card’s expiry is a month a lawfully present spouse cannot work. None of these nefarious, underhanded schemes, too numerous to count, appears in the Federal Register. The Oversight Committee can demand the staffing figures, the internal guidance and the emails behind these slowdowns, and put the officials responsible under oath. Like noxious black mould, furtive toxicity withers in daylight; dispelling secrecy is an important antidote,” Khanna emphasises.
The incoming Congress may be able to subject immigration policy to greater scrutiny and use funding negotiations to press the administration. But with executive authority intact and major disputes continuing in the courts, the practical impact on H-1B workers, students, H-4 spouses and employment-based green card applicants will depend largely on how those legal and regulatory battles unfold.

Could Hyrox's Olympic ambition spell the end for triathlon?
- Published
"Our biggest concern is that they're not just here to take part, they're here to take over."
British triathlete Max Stapley first saw the news on Instagram. Last week, World Triathlon announced it was partnering with Hyrox - the fitness craze which combines running with exercise stations.
The agreement means Hyrox becomes a recognised discipline within World Triathlon. And now it sits under a recognised international federation, it could be eligible for inclusion at the Olympics and Paralympics.
It is too late for the Los Angeles 2028 Games but is there room for both hybrid racing and triathlon to feature at a future Olympics? Or could one replace the other?
For triathlon, a sport which has been in the Olympics since 2000, and has long-established professional circuits, its athletes are questioning whether they'll reap any rewards from this partnership - or even, whether it could "kill" the sport altogether.
'We were kind of blindsided'
Stapley, who spoke to BBC Sport from a training camp in Thailand, was having dinner with friends when his phone started pinging with news of the proposals and reaction to them.
"I was like, hold on a minute, what's this?", said Stapley.
"We don't even get an early notification, we found out on Instagram".
The post read, external: 'Hyrox x World Triathlon are officially introducing 'Hybrid Racing' as a new discipline within the World Triathlon family.'
Sophie Evans - who won gold as part of England's Commonwealth Games mixed relay team in Birmingham in 2022 - said she was "surprised" to receive the news like that.
"I'm not actually against it being part of World Triathlon. It's more the fact we were blindsided, it's just like it's here," she added.
Stapley accused World Triathlon of not caring about its athletes because he did not receive any communication from his sport's governing body prior to and after the announcement was made.
"They have no respect for us," he said. "They don't even contact us like 'hey, do you guys actually care about this, or what do you think?'"
In response, a World Triathlon spokesperson told BBC Sport: "The World Triathlon Executive Board approved the partnership. The board includes representatives of the World Triathlon Athletes' Committee elected by their peers.
"Athlete representatives are involved in every executive board discussion, and their voice is always heard.
"The announcement was communicated through the same procedures followed for all World Triathlon releases."
'An attack on our existence'
World Triathlon says the partnership is designed to "benefit the entire World Triathlon movement",, external with new opportunities to engage athletes and audiences, and a stronger platform to grow triathlon and multisport from grassroots to elite level.
The question for athletes is, how?
European champion Roksana Slupek, of Poland, said she was "not against the idea", but wanted more information.
"What's the benefit for us, for triathlon? It's nothing against Hyrox," said Slupek.
However, Stapley called the move an "attack on our whole existence" and is concerned that World Triathlon could direct attention and resources towards Hyrox's Olympic ambition - at the expense of his own sport.
"How does Hyrox grow triathlon? If anything they've killed triathlon," he said, while also suggesting brands would rather get in early with Hyrox athletes before they potentially appear at an Olympics.
"Sponsorships have reduced because there's no visibility on TV, you have to pay to watch us.
"We are triathletes that do the short distance, which is the Olympic distance, and we've trained all our lives for it.
"There's no swimming, there's no biking, it's indoors. [Hyrox] has got nothing to do [with triathlon]".
"It seems like our sport's gone, 'no worries, come along, use our structure, use our access to the International Olympic Committee, and perhaps take our space'.
"We've got an opportunity to win medals in Los Angeles [at the 2028 Olympics], but will we have it further down the track?"
Evans said that while triathlon was an "established" Olympic sport, that has provided high quality racing since its introduction to the Games 26 years ago, this new partnership has introduced a "level of uncertainty".
"A lot of the resistance has come from athletes, because you don't know," she added.
A World Triathlon spokesperson told BBC Sport, it is continuing to "increase its focus and involvement in the Olympic and Paralympic families" and that it is in the "planning phase" for Brisbane 2032, adding that "triathlon is, and will remain, at the heart of everything we do".
BBC Sport approached Hyrox for comment, but they referred us to the statements made by World Triathlon.
Can triathlon and Hybrid racing co-exist?
Sam Dickinson - who won an Olympic triathlon bronze in Paris as part Team GB's relay quartet - can see why the move makes sense but wants more clarity.
"It's trying to get people active not from an elite side but from a participation side," Dickinson told BBC Sport.
"So in that sense it does make sense that as a multi-sport it comes under the World Triathlon umbrella.
"But it's early days, we don't have any of the bread and butter of exactly what's going on."
And there lies the crux of the problem - the lack of clarity has fuelled speculation about what the future holds.
World Triathlon does have other disciplines in its remit, such as Aquathlon and duathlon.
BBC Sport has been told that 'Fitness Racing' was first included as a discipline in the World Triathlon Constitution in October 2025, a move supported by the majority of the governing body's National Federations.
A World Triathlon spokesperson added that the partnership provides opportunities to 'reach new audiences' through collaborating with global partners.
Founded in 2017, Hyrox's popularity has continued to grow rapidly. A total of 1.5m athletes took part during the 2025/26 season - up from 650,000 the year before - with participation projected to surpass 2m in the current season.
British Triathlon, one of World Triathlon's national federations, told BBC Sport it recognises "World Triathlon's work to grow, develop and strengthen the sport of triathlon, multi-sport and its community", but is waiting to hear the "full operational, governance and commercial framework" for the partnership.

India successfully test-fires indigenously developed quasi-ballistic missile Pralay | Watch
Pralay, developed by the DRDO, is a short-range surface-to-surface missile with a payload capacity of 500-1,000 kg.
India on Thursday successfully test-fired quasi-ballistic missile Pralay from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the coast of Odisha. The missile, developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), is capable of carrying conventional warheads, the defence ministry said in a statement.
Pralay is a short-range surface-to-surface missile with a payload capacity of 500-1,000 kg. "With this successful test, the induction of the system has become imminent," the ministry said.
Defence minister Rajnath Singh also complimented DRDO, Defence Forces and industry partners on the successful flight-test and said the missile equipped with advanced technologies will further enhance the technological capabilities and operational preparedness of the military against emerging threats.
“The test was conducted as part of user evaluation trials and successfully met all the stipulated objectives, as validated by data captured through various range instruments. This successful trial marks another significant milestone in strengthening India’s indigenous defence capabilities,” Singh wrote in a post on X.
The defence ministry said that all the test objectives were fully met as confirmed by the test data captured by various range instruments deployed by Integrated Test Range, Chandipur.
Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad, along with other DRDO laboratories, indigenously developed the missile, it said.
Bharat Dynamics Limited, one of the development-cum-production-partners, has produced the system.
The flight-test was conducted in the presence of senior officials from DRDO, representatives from the industry and the defence forces, as part of user evaluation trials, the ministry said in a statement.

Quick Answer
Your iPhone Duo can do more than multitask! These 10 quirky apps turn the foldable into a retro computer, cassette player, Nintendo DS, accordion, instant camera, virtual fridge, and even a grilled cheese toaster. Some are free, others paid, but all make clever, fun use of its folding design.
The iPhone Duo is perhaps the most radically different iPhone since the original iPhone. While its arrival was rumored for over a year, Apple finally launched it this September. The phone can fold in half to become nearly passport-sized and can be unfolded to shape-shift into a bigger, tablet-ish smartphone. Ever since its launch, we have been constantly hearing about its multitasking prowess, its computer-like processing abilities, how well it handles productivity apps, yada yada yada…
But all this is pretty basic, something we expect with all new iPhones, or rather flagship smartphones at this point. With the kind of price and specs these high-end smartphones come with, it hardly is a surprise that they can handle power-hungry tasks with ease. The foldable form-factor and the added display real estate make it a different experience, surely. But surely there is way more to the device than the same old tasks and apps? So, we are on a mission to make your iPhone Duo fun, using all that processing and multitasking magic that it possesses.
The result is these ten apps.
They are not at all useful. But they make the Duo a-not-just-another-serious (read: boring) device out there. They add an element to it that we all so need to survive – they make it fun. Got an iPhone Duo? Download! (Note: relax, all of these are optimized for the iPhone Duo)
Table of Contents
Top 10 Wacky and Fun iPhone Duo Apps
| Sl No | App | Price | What it does | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tiny Computer | $3.99 | Turns the Duo into a retro PC with vintage keyboards, games, and interfaces. | 
| 2 | Deck Man | $4.99 | Recreates a cassette Walkman with realistic tape controls and sounds. | 
| 3 | MD Vinyl | Free | Turns the screen into a vinyl turntable with spinning records and music controls. | 
| 4 | Fold Accordion | $2.99 | Uses the folding hinge as accordion bellows to create music. | 
| 5 | Delta | Free | Recreates the Nintendo DS gaming experience with dual-screen controls. | 
| 6 | Toastie | $2.99 | Turns the Duo into a virtual grilled cheese maker that works when folded shut. | 
| 7 | TypeDraw | $4.99 | Recreates a paper notebook with handwriting, page turns, and paper effects. | 
| 8 | Snapshots | $1.99 | Turns the Duo into a Polaroid-style instant camera with developing photos. | 
| 9 | Phridge | Free | Creates a virtual fridge you can decorate, stock, and mess around with. | 
| 10 | ChompDuo | Free | Adds six animated monsters whose jaws open and close as you fold the phone. | 
Tiny Computer (USD 3.99): Unfolding Retro computer feels
Imagine getting a vintage PC feel on something as new and pristine as the iPhone Duo? That is exactly what the app Tiny Computer can deliver. Using the half-fold setting of the iPhone Duo, the app turns your phone into a proper vintage computer. The upper half of the screen becomes the display while the lower half becomes the keyboard. You get to choose from ten different computers in total, including the Apple Macintosh, IBM PC, iMac G3, IBM ThinkPad, Windows XP, Amiga 500, and more.
It is not just all show; you can actually use some retro paint apps, run old command-line interfaces, play games like Solitaire, and even type on clicky keyboards. Each machine also hides secret commands and files paired with occasional crashes to make the whole experience even more believable.
Deck Man (USD 4.99): Go cassette crazy!
Another app that brings retro feels to the Duo is the Deck Man. It is one of the most visually appealing apps for the Duo because it essentially turns your iPhone Duo into a 1980s cassette Walkman player. The app uses the unfolded version of the phone as the collection of cassettes in your music library that you can browse. You then “insert” the cassette of your choice into the deck, and once you fold it, the secondary screen mimics the look of a cassette Walkman player.
The app has realistic mechanical clicks, background tape static, and if you fast-forward or rewind it too aggressively, the virtual tape inside can get all tangled and then would have to be untangled manually, just like a retro cassette player. “Tape” this one to your Duo!
MD Vinyl (Free): Spin those discs!
If cassettes are “too” modern for you, then you can go even further back in the music era with the iPhone Duo by installing MD Vinyl. This essentially turns the Duo into a virtual turntable with spinning records and album art. The record design determines the aesthetics of the app. The app allows you to pick and drop the needle to play or pause the tracks. It can pair with music apps like Apple Music and Spotify. It is not a new app and has existed for years, but it attains a whole new dimension on the Duo, adding a vintage touch to the modern audio experience.
Fold Accordion (USD 2.99): Fold and unfold to create music
If there is one app that makes the most use of the iPhone Duo’s form factor, it is the Fold Accordion. It literally turns the hinge of the iPhone Duo into working accordion bellows. When you launch the app, it places the keys on the display, which you can press with your right hand while opening and closing the Duo with the left hand to create music of your own. The app comes with a learning mode which highlights keys you have to press to create something pleasant, instead of getting straight to the chaos of keys. A great way to test that folding mechanism too.
Delta (Nintendo DS) (free): Double screen gaming magic, DS style!
Popular Retro Game emulator Delta has launched an updated version of its app, specifically for the iPhone Duo. The app brings specially designed skins for the iPhone Duo, and the most interesting one of the lot is the Nintendo DS portable gaming console, which interestingly was the world’s first mainstream foldable device. The app uses the inner display of the iPhone Duo to bring a DS-style layout and controls across the displays. The game even enters sleep state when the device is folded, similar to the Nintendo DS. Trust the Duo to bring back the magic of double-screen gaming.
Toastie (USD 2.99): Smartest thing since sliced bread!
Unleash the inner chef in you with the absolutely useless but equally fun app called Toastie. This app turns the iPhone Duo into a – wait for it – virtual grilled cheese toaster. You get 15 seconds to assemble your sandwich, and once you are done, you have to hit the ‘grill’ button and physically close the iPhone Duo shut. You then have to wait, listen to the sizzle, or get a slight peek to ensure your toastie is grilling well. If you open the phone too soon, the cheese won’t be melted; if you wait too long, it might end up getting burned. Once you are done with it, you serve it, and you get a star based on your accuracy, recipe, timing, and so on. Useful? Not. But definitely the smartest thing since sliced bread. Actually, the smartest thing done to sliced bread!
TypeDraw (USD 4.99): Paper-like Moleskine
The iPhone Duo looks like a handy pocket notebook or a passport, and TypeDraw literally converts it into a handy little Moleskine-like notebook. It even comes with a digital thread, just like you find on a notebook, which you have to move or swipe aside to open the notebook (or just open the Duo). You can write anywhere on a page using an Apple Pencil or your finger and can even fiddle and curl up paper corners, as well as choose fonts (you can convert your handwriting into one, if you wish), types of paper, and even plain, ruled, dotted, or grid patterns on paper. And the page turns on the internal display are absolutely paper-like. It is like carrying a real notebook.
Snapshots ($1.99): Unfold to Polaroid
Snapshots is an app that helps your Duo morph into an instant camera. It is one of the very first community-developed apps optimized specifically for the iPhone Duo. When bent in half (90 degrees), the top half of the primary display becomes the viewfinder while the bottom half holds the controls. Once you hit the shutter, the photo captured on the upper half of the viewfinder is virtually printed on the lower half with the same mechanical sound and effect as on an instant camera. Just like with a real instant camera, the photo does not appear right away but takes a few seconds to develop, giving us those Polaroid feels.
Phridge (free): Chill…literally!
This is perhaps the most quirky and our personal favorite app in the list. It turns the iPhone Duo into a – wait for it – refrigerator. When folded, you can decorate the ‘door’ of this fridge with magnets, to-do lists, photographs. And when you open it, you can see groceries and food and drink inside and arrange them. This is when the real fun happens, because you can topple something over, drop a fizzy drink, or break a glass jar or bottle. You can also place your hand in a slingshot to shoot stones at the shelves, or get a sword to slice things in half, if you feel like some chaos. You can only close the fridge when you fold the phone shut, making the hinge integral to its operation. How cool is that? Just chillin…
Chompduo (Free): Jaw-dropping (and closing) stuff!
We all need an app that adds six hungry monsters to your iPhone Duo. Well, we do, anyway. That is exactly what ChompDuo does. When installed, it unleashes six hungry monsters on your Duo that open their huge mouths when the device is unfolded, making the inner display a giant mouth. You can tap on the open mouth to make it bite or drag it to squeeze it shut. When you fold the phone, the jaws close shut with a chomp sound, and a pair of googly eyes appear on the outer display, which can jump when you tap on them. What more does one need on a foldable?

Manufacturing corporate sector’s GVA grows 9.28% in FY25: Govt survey
Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh emerged as the five largest contributors to manufacturing GVA
The gross value added (GVA) of India’s manufacturing corporate sector grew 9.28% in 2024-25, while the number of factories in operation and total employment increased by 3.45% and 7.57%, respectively, according to the latest Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) released by the ministry of statistics and programme implementation on Wednesday.
The manufacturing corporate sector accounted for more than 89% of the total GVA during the financial year, underlining its dominant contribution to the country’s registered industrial output.
The survey also recorded a 7.25% increase in the gross value of plant and machinery in the registered manufacturing sector over the previous year. Net value added per factory in operation rose 6.59%, while GVA per person engaged increased by 2.25%.
Also Read | India’s manufacturing growth momentum eases in Oct
The ministry released Volume I and the Summary Results of Factory Sector of ASI 2024-25, along with unit-level data and metadata, providing a detailed picture of the performance, investment patterns, employment and output of India’s registered manufacturing sector.
The five leading industries — food products, textiles, basic metals, motor vehicles and wearing apparel — together accounted for more than 41% of total manufacturing employment during 2024-25.
Geographically, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh emerged as the five largest contributors to manufacturing GVA, collectively accounting for more than 54% of the national total.
The survey highlighted a significant concentration of capital and production among larger factories. Units with investment of ₹10 crore or more in plant and machinery constituted 15.84% of operational factories but accounted for 87.42% of total fixed capital, 59.66% of employment, 76.82% of gross output and 78.07% of net value added.
Also Read | Solving Make in India’s aluminium conundrum
In contrast, factories with investment of up to ₹5 crore represented 78.69% of operational units. However, their contribution to fixed capital was 10.55%, while they accounted for 34.32% of persons engaged, 19.24% of total output and 17.61% of net value added.
A similar concentration was evident when factories were classified by output. Units producing more than ₹10 crore worth of output accounted for 47.63% of operational factories but contributed 98.10% of total output and 97.87% of net value added. They also accounted for 95.55% of fixed capital and 88.78% of employment.
The ASI is the principal source of industrial statistics on the organised manufacturing sector and provides information on capital formation, employment, wages, input costs, output and value addition. Its findings are also used in compiling national and state-level national accounts statistics.
Also Read | Indian manufacturing is learning to produce better, not just more
The detailed publications supplement the factsheet released on September 30, 2026, and provide results at the national, state and industry levels. Volume I contains detailed factory-sector statistics classified according to the National Industrial Classification (NIC), 2008, while the summary publication presents key indicators of industrial performance across states and Union territories.
The survey covers registered factories, certain bidi and cigar manufacturing establishments, electricity undertakings and eligible establishments with 100 or more employees. Data are collected electronically through a dedicated web portal.

Reimagining the psychological warfare of Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? as a home-invasion thriller, Killing Time “follows a couple on the run following a bank robbery and murder spree who seek refuge in the home of an affluent married couple. But as the night unfolds, the fugitives discover that their seemingly well-heeled hosts harbor secrets of their own, setting the stage for a volatile confrontation in which the lines between predator and prey become increasingly blurred.”
The film marks the final production from producer Linda Duncombe, who passed away last month.
Watch on Deadline
Pic is produced by Larry Greenberg, Eric Brenner, Raja Collins, Linda Duncombe, German Michael Torres and Joshua Friedman. Executive producers are Berry Meyerowitz, Jeff Sackman and Eduard Osipov.
“Killing Time is a tribute to the hard work and dedication of producer Linda Duncombe, who tragically passed away last month” said Quiver’s Larry Greenberg, “We have been developing this project for five years, and it finally took the passion of star Freddie Prinze Jr., who worked with Quiver on 2024’s surprise hit The Girl in the Pool, and the vision of director Joshua Friedman to bring it to life.”
“Freddie, Shelley, Sasha, and William brought everything this film needed — charm, menace, and the ability to turn on a dime” said director Joshua Friedman, “Watching them go at each other across a living room was the whole movie. As for Linda, she believed in this film from the start and fought beside me to get it made — and for that this film will always be sacred to me.”

The measure, which may face legal challenges, requires girls who want to play in girls' sports to produce documentation from a healthcare provider who has verified "the student's biological sex" relying on the student's reproductive anatomy — in other words, a genital exam — genetic makeup or their natural testosterone levels. Due to how expensive genetic and testosterone testing can be, the genital exams are the most accessible option.
In the aftermath of Election Day, social media users circulated a rumor that Washington voters passed an anti-trans measure that would allegedly subject girls who want to play school sports in the state to genital inspections. 
The rumor spread on X, Threads and Bluesky. Some posts shared additional alleged context, claiming that the ballot measure would subject children who want to play in girls' sports to genital inspections. Others dismissed these claims as a "fantasy."
Washington voters did, in fact, pass a measure called Initiative 26-638 aimed at banning trans girls from playing in girls' sports. The act requires medical providers to "verify" a student's biological sex using reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup or naturally produced testosterone levels.
In theory, the law does not explicitly require genital exams for anyone because it provides three options for sex verification. In practice, due to how expensive genetic and testosterone testing can be, the genital exams are the most accessible option, according to child advocacy groups and medical providers who oppose the provision.
It is worth noting these tests cannot necessarily definitively determine a person's biological sex, which scientists say is a complex category.
The measure subjects every girl who wishes to play in girls' school sports to sex verification, but does not subject students who wish to participate in boys' sports to the same scrutiny. The Washington Interscholastic Activities Association reportedly said earlier this year that it was aware of 10 trans student athletes total in the state; it's unclear how many of these athletes are trans boys, as opposed to trans girls. 
While the Washington secretary of state website indicates that there are still ballots left to count, as of this writing, support for the measure has a 13-point lead over opposition. Furthermore, The Associated Press called the race, stating that the "Yes" vote won.
Snopes, like many credible media publications, relies on AP calls for elections. As such, we have rated this claim as true.
(Some posts stated that the measure was "winning" or had won before AP called the race; ultimately, those posts turned out to be true, even if they called the race early.)
It's worth noting that the act may face legal challenges.
"Many have said that I-638 is likely unconstitutional and we understand there are legal groups and organizations considering litigation," said No Hate in WA State, the main coalition opposing the measure. The American Civil Liberties Union-Washington said in its own statement that it was "exploring all potential next steps to uphold the rights of transgender girls and their access to school sports."
I-638's text, examined
The complete text for I-638 is available on the Washington secretary of state's website. Here's the relevant section (emphasis ours):
NEW SECTION. Sec. 3. A new section is added to chapter 28A.600 RCW to read as follows:
(1) Policies, procedures, rules, and other requirements adopted in accordance with RCW 28A.600.200 by a school district board of directors or a voluntary nonprofit entity must prohibit biologically male students from competing with and against female students in athletic activities with separate classifications for male and female students if the athletic activity is:
(a) Intended for female students only; and
(b) An individual or team competition activity.
(2) A student who elects to participate in individual or team competition activities intended for female students only governed under subsection (1) of this section shall provide, as part of the required routine sports physical examination, a health examination and consent form or other statement signed by the student's personal health care provider that verifies the student's biological sex, relying only on one or more of the following: The student's reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup, or normal endogenously produced testosterone levels.
As opponents to I-638 have noted, a birth certificate would not be an acceptable form of sex verification under I-638. About 28% of K-12 school-age girls in Washington do not have a personal doctor or nurse, meaning that it's likely many families would not be able to rely on an established medical history with a health care provider.
The nonpartisan Washington State Parent Teacher Association, the largest volunteer and child advocacy organization in the state, opposed I-638 on the grounds that it would likely require many girls to either undergo an intimate, embarrassing and medically unnecessary genital examination or forgo playing in girls' sports. Here's what the organization said (emphasis ours):
Two of the three permitted methods, genetic testing and testosterone measurement, are expensive and unlikely to be covered by insurance for this purpose, since neither is clinically indicated. That makes an examination of reproductive anatomy the most accessible pathway for most families.
The burden falls hardest on rural, uninsured, and lower-income families, and on families without an established relationship with a healthcare provider — who face the added problem that the measure never says what qualifies someone as a student's "personal health care provider."
Doctors and medical professionals opposing the initiative shared similar warnings and noted that major medical organizations advise against pelvic exams for adolescent girls, with some citing psychological harms and potential future avoidance of medical care. The Washington Academy of Family Physicians and the Washington State Nurses Association opposed the measure.
The Seattle Times reported that doctors may interpret the measure differently, given that it's vague and, in some views, "poorly written."

France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation
- Published
Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators are expected to take part in marches across France as five unions join strikes and protests in a national day of action.
The protests began in September with high school students complaining about poor conditions and resources in education, but have spread to include the so-called "yellow-vest" movement and workers.
Authorities expect 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators to join marches, with tens of thousands more in Paris alone, in a day billed by one union leader as "a great day of convergence".
The five unions have combined forces across the public and private sector, with demands for higher wages to combat the cost of living and protected public services.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has said that 70,000 police and gendarmes are being deployed, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence.
More than 250 separate actions are planned for 5 November, with some disruption reported in schools, hospitals and public transport.
Workers have also been asked to halt production at oil refineries, and France is expected to import more electricity than it produces on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants.
A coalition of unions has urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government. In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, or Smic, which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour.
The head of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, complained that it was not just the minimum wage that needed to increase: "We are asking for a net increase of €100 a month."
The government has sought to appease public anger over rising prices, bringing down the cost of fuel by releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopular Parcoursup university admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028.
Some 81 lycées - high schools that cater for 15-18 year-olds - were shut on Thursday morning, according to the education ministry. It added that about 17.5% of primary schools too were affected by the strikes.
Large numbers are expected on the streets, especially in the capital, and Léon said she would be happy if 800,000 people turned out.
One union leader Sophie Binet, who called it the "great day of convergence", added: "The time has come to take the mobilisation to the next level; the strike must take over."
Meanwhile, a revived gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement that staged a revolt against the high cost of living several years ago has called for further blockades and protests on Friday and Saturday too.
Union leaders have complained that recent marches have been kept away from the centre of Paris, because of violence that broke out in towns and cities on 17 October and led to more than 2,000 stores being looted and historic buildings being set on fire.
Thursday's march will be allowed through the centre of Paris, although not along the route proposed by the unions between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Concorde, which would have taken protesters near the National Assembly, the Élysée Palace, and the prime minister's residence at Hôtel Matignon.
Instead, the march is set to follow another central route from Place de la République to Place de la Nation. The CFDT union complained that getting court approval for the route only on Wednesday evening made organising the march more difficult.
The last big mobilisation at the weekend passed off with relatively little violence, and the interior minister said the police deployment would be on a similar scale on Thursday. Nuñez has spoken of three potential risks on Thursday, from radical left "black blocs" groups and looting to wildcat marches without union authorisation.

The Indian Council of Medical Research has funded a four-year study to investigate the genetic and immunological mechanisms underlying autoimmune diseases by studying families with multiple affected members, AIIMS doctors said on Thursday, appealing to SLE patients to get enrolled in the study.
The project titled ‘Genomic Profiling and Identification of Targetable Shared Immunopathogenic Events in Multiplex Families with Autoimmune Diseases’ has been awarded to Dipyaman Ganguly of Ashoka University, Sonipat, Haryana, and Ranjan Gupta, additional professor in the Department of Rheumatology, AIIMS, Delhi.
The study aims to build a nationwide cohort of 200 families in which multiple members are affected by autoimmune diseases. Each participating family must have at least one member diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), commonly known as lupus, Gupta said.
The researchers will conduct genetic and immunological assessments of the enrolled patients and their family members to identify shared biological mechanisms that contribute to the development of these conditions.
The findings could help scientists better understand the disease processes involved and identify potential targets for developing new therapies, he said.
Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own tissues. A family history of such conditions is associated with an increased risk of developing them, highlighting the importance of investigating genetic and shared immunological factors, Gupta said.
The four-year project will involve clinical centres at AIIMS Delhi; AIIMS Bibinagar, Telangana; Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGIMS), Lucknow; St John's Hospital, Bengaluru; Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad; and the Kolkata Medical College. These centres will contribute clinical data and biological samples for the study.
Patients diagnosed with lupus and residing in Delhi-NCR can contact the centre at AIIMS Delhi to check their eligibility for participation, Gupta said.
Participation will be subject to eligibility assessment and the study's enrolment requirements.

Preparations for next year’s 39th National Games in Meghalaya are progressing well, said Games Technical Conduct Committee (GTCC) chairperson Sunaina Kumari on Thursday.
“We are satisfied with the progress so far,” Kumari told reporters after a four-day inspection of proposed venues in Shillong and Jowai.
The five-member GTCC, appointed by the Indian Olympic Association on October 14, visited Meghalaya from November 2 to 5. Kumari praised the coordination among government departments and agencies.
“Everyone is working together towards one common goal, which is to ensure the successful hosting of the Games,” she said. She also thanked Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma, the Deputy Chief Ministers and Sports Minister Dr Vijay Kumar.
Meghalaya has proposed 39 disciplines across Shillong, Jowai and Tura, but the list is tentative, and the IOA will make the final decision with the GTCC. Taekwondo’s inclusion is also subject to the IOA’s decision.
Proposed venues include the JN Sports Complex, which would host the opening ceremony, Shillong Golf Club, North-Eastern Hill University campus and Umiam Lake. The dates are yet to be announced.

upGrad has filed an insolvency petition against B9 Beverages Ltd, the maker of Bira91 beer, over alleged unpaid dues of ₹1.02 Cr, adding to the financial and legal challenges facing the brewer. The petition, filed under Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016, was submitted to the Delhi bench of the NCLT on October 22, as per documents reviewed by Moneycontrol. upGrad has named B9 Beverages as the corporate debtor and sought the initiation of the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) to recover the outstanding amount. The petition does not disclose the nature of services provided by upGrad to the beverage maker. Inc42 has reached out to upGrad and Anicut Capital for a comment on the development. The story will be updated on receiving a response. The filing comes amid mounting liabilities and creditor disputes at B9 Beverages, which is facing insolvency-related action from multiple creditors. In September, the NCLT directed B9 Beverages and its creditors to explore a settlement through mediation in connection with multiple insolvency proceedings. The tribunal also restrained the brewer from disposing of its assets while discussions were underway. The company has also faced action from glass manufacturer Hindusthan National Glass & Industries Ltd (HNGIL), which sought to recover ₹11.8 Cr in alleged unpaid dues. HNGIL issued a demand notice under Section 8 of the IBC over customised glass bottles manufactured against confirmed purchase orders but allegedly not collected by the brewer. The glassmaker claimed that more than 51 Lakh bottles worth over ₹7 Cr remained stored at its facilities, despite it encashing bank guarantees worth ₹3.91 Cr. The latest development comes as the startup attempts to restructure its business amid a prolonged financial crisis. In July, founder Ankur Jain stepped down from the company's board and relinquished executive control and ownership following a dispute with investors and lenders. VC firm Anicut Capital, one of Bira's key lenders, subsequently took control of Jain and his family's stake in the company, as per reports. Anicut had extended loans to B9 Beverages between 2017 and 2022, secured against the promoter family's stake. The brewer is now expected to be recapitalised by existing investors and lenders under a revival plan aimed at clearing statutory, employee and vendor dues and restarting operations. Founded by Jain in 2015, Bira 91 raised more than $200 Mn from investors. Its annual revenue crossed $100 Mn in FY23. Its shareholders include Peak XV Partners, Sofina and Japan-based Kirin Holdings. Anicut Capital and Hero Corporate Services' family office are among its key lenders. Its troubles began after it converted into a public company, triggering fresh excise approval requirements across multiple states. This disrupted the production and sales of the beer. The company subsequently wrote off inventory worth around ₹80 Cr and fell behind on vendor payments. The company eventually paused its packaged beer business amid a prolonged funding crunch, mounting vendor liabilities and difficulties in meeting employee and statutory obligations. The company reported a net loss of ₹748 Cr in FY24, with accumulated losses of ₹2,117.9 Cr. Its auditor also warned that current liabilities exceeded assets by ₹487 Cr as of March 2024. Under Section 9 of the IBC, an operational creditor can approach the NCLT to initiate insolvency proceedings after serving a demand notice and meeting the prescribed statutory conditions. However, filing a petition does not automatically trigger insolvency proceedings. The NCLT will examine the application to determine whether the requirements for admission have been met.

Hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws in an attempt to hack visitors of multiple websites, including one celebrating the 250th anniversary of American independence, researchers said Wednesday.
The attackers, which the researchers assessed with “moderate to high confidence” were part of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service, targeted other sites, many with links to that country’s ongoing war against Ukraine. The attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites. JavaScript injected into the traffic then profiled the device. The final payloads, tailored to the type of platform visiting, attempted to steal browser cookies and, in some cases, Wi-Fi passwords and full mobile device data.
Wielding DarkSword
One of the impersonated sites was america250.org, belonging to a non-partisan group of lawmakers, business executives, and at least one former member of the Trump administration. The attackers registered america250[.]holiday and used it as a reverse proxy to america250.org. The imposter website delivered content from the real one that added malicious JavaScript into it.
“We assess that the intrusion set may have deliberately selected this website due to its association with a high-profile national celebration, potentially leveraging the event as a pretext for invitation-themed spear-phishing campaigns,” researchers from security firm Sekoia said.
A second website, theowo[.]club, proxied the website Raffles of London OWO, a luxury hotel physically close to some of the UK’s most sensitive government institutions, including the Ministry of Defence and 10 Downing Street, the official residence and office of the British Prime Minister. Open source reporting indicates that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stayed there during a visit on October 14.

India’s anaemia burden is not in doubt. The fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) found that more than half of women and about two-thirds of young children are anaemic. In this context, double-fortified salt (DFS) — fortified with iodine and iron — is often proposed as a potentially transformative solution. However, the case for DFS rests on convenience: everyone consumes salt, so why not add iron to it? But convenience is not efficacy, and a policy that asks the country to continue consuming salt to deliver iron deserves closer scrutiny.
Iron fortification of salt is a vehicle that cuts against public health. Indians consume, by most estimates, roughly twice the five grams of salt a day recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO). About one in three adults has hypertension, and India’s own non-communicable disease (NCD) action plan commits to a 30% relative reduction in salt intake.

Insurtech Go Digit reported a 31.1% year-on-year (YoY) decline in its net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) to ₹142.4 Cr from ₹206.8 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. The insurtech major's profit also declined 62.4% sequentially from ₹378.61 Cr in the June quarter. The decline in profitability came despite a marginal increase in insurance revenue, which rose 1.7% to ₹2,720.5 Cr during the quarter from ₹2,674.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, insurance revenue increased 2.1% from ₹2,665.6 Cr. Segment-wise, Motor Third Party (TP) insurance remained Go Digit's largest business, contributing ₹1,066.1 Cr to insurance revenue in Q2 FY27, up 8.3% YoY. Motor Own Damage (OD) insurance revenue grew at a faster pace of 11.4% YoY to ₹640.64 Cr. The company's gross written premium for the quarter dipped by 3.6% YoY to ₹2,571 Cr while gross direct premium, dipped 1.2% to ₹2,351 Cr. However, the company's insurance service result, which reflects the profitability of its insurance operations before investment and other financial income, sunk 73.4% YoY to ₹43 Cr from ₹161.98 Cr in the year-ago quarter. The figure also fell 62.3% sequentially from ₹114 Cr. The deterioration in the insurance service result came as insurance service expenses increased 22.4% YoY to ₹2,607.73 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹2,130.85 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. Incurred claims rose 9.2% to ₹1,968.03 Cr from ₹1,802.96 Cr, while employee benefit expenses increased 4.3% to ₹95.48 Cr. Commission expenses, on the other hand, declined 2.6% YoY to ₹781.88 Cr from ₹803.10 Cr. Other insurance service expenses increased 1.7% to ₹94.52 Cr. On the investment front, Go Digit reported a 20.6% YoY increase in investment income to ₹368.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹305.5 Cr in the year-ago period. However, investment income declined 39.2% sequentially from ₹606.47 Cr. The company's net finance result, which includes investment income and insurance finance income or expenses, increased 28.6% YoY to ₹196.94 Cr. Consequently, Go Digit's profit before tax (PBT) declined 31.2% YoY to ₹190.18 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹276.30 Cr in Q2 FY26. The figure was also down 62.4% sequentially from ₹505.96 Cr in Q1 FY27. Total tax expense stood at ₹47.79 Cr during the quarter, comprising current tax of ₹3.93 Cr and deferred tax of ₹43.86 Cr. This compared with a total tax expense of ₹69.51 Cr in Q2 FY26. For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), Go Digit reported a 3.2% YoY decline in net profit to ₹521 Cr from ₹538.23 Cr in H1 FY26. Insurance revenue increased 4.5% YoY to ₹5,386.09 Cr during the six-month period. Shares of Go Digit ended today’s trading session 1.05% higher at ₹260.30.

Afcon to return to two-year cycle after Caf U-turn
- Published
The Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle after a U-turn from the Confederation of African Football (Caf).
In December, Caf announced that the tournament would be held every four years instead, but that decision has been reversed after a review.
Under the new plans, the governing body was planning an African Nations League to replace Afcon as its biennial tournament, but acknowledged that it would take several years to generate the revenue required to become self-sufficient.
"The decision by the Executive Committee to reinstate the organisation of the Afcon every two years aims to advance, protect and promote the interests of African football and the 54 Caf Member Associations, as well as those of African players playing for clubs outside the continent," Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in a statement.
The biennial hosting of Afcon has long caused issues with the football calendar, with the vast majority of recent tournaments held midway through the European club season.
Fifa's expanded 32-team Club World Cup was held in June and July last year, which also forced Caf to opt for mid-season dates.
The next Afcon will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament, followed by editions in 2028, 2031 and 2033. There will be no tournament in 2030 because of the World Cup.
The dramatic 2025 Afcon final saw Senegal crowned champions before they were stripped of their title three months later in favour of Morocco.
